process_mapping: squads/research/workflows/tech-research/tech-research-pipeline.yaml

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# OPERATIONAL CONFIG (preserved from v1.1.0)
# These sections are read by Phase 3.7 (playwright) and Phase 3 (search waves).
# They are NOT SINKRA metadata — they are runtime configuration.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Playwright Deep Research Phase Configuration
playwright_deep_research:
  enabled: true
  description: |
    Browser automation phase that queries multiple LLMs (Grok, Claude.ai, Gemini)
    for deep research when traditional search doesn't achieve sufficient coverage.

  # Trigger conditions
  auto_trigger_threshold: 0.70  # coverage score below this triggers deep research
  manual_trigger_keywords:
    - "--deep"
    - "*deep"
    - "multiple perspectives"
    - "compare LLM views"
    - "cross-reference with LLMs"

  # Timing configuration
  timeout_per_llm: 60  # seconds to wait for each LLM response
  retry_count: 2       # retries per LLM if first attempt fails
  retry_delay: 5       # seconds between retries

  # LLM configurations
  llms:
    - name: grok
      url: https://grok.x.ai
      enabled: true
      priority: 1
      selectors:
        chat_input_primary: "textarea[placeholder*='Ask']"
        chat_input_fallback_1: "textarea"
        chat_input_fallback_2: "[contenteditable='true']"
        submit_button_primary: "button[type='submit']"
        submit_button_fallback_1: "button[aria-label*='Send']"
        submit_button_fallback_2: "button:has-text('Send')"
        response_container_primary: "[data-testid='message-content']"
        response_container_fallback_1: ".message-content"
        response_container_fallback_2: "[class*='response']"
        login_indicator_primary: "[data-testid='user-menu']"
        login_indicator_fallback_1: "img[alt*='avatar']"
        login_indicator_fallback_2: "[class*='user-profile']"
      notes: "Requires X/Twitter login. UI may change frequently."

    - name: claude
      url: https://claude.ai
      enabled: true
      priority: 2
      selectors:
        chat_input_primary: "div[contenteditable='true']"
        chat_input_fallback_1: "[data-testid='chat-input']"
        chat_input_fallback_2: "textarea"
        submit_button_primary: "button[aria-label='Send message']"
        submit_button_fallback_1: "button[type='submit']"
        submit_button_fallback_2: "button:has-text('Send')"
        response_container_primary: "[data-testid='assistant-message']"
        response_container_fallback_1: ".assistant-message"
        response_container_fallback_2: "[class*='response']"
        login_indicator_primary: "button[data-testid='account-menu']"
        login_indicator_fallback_1: "[class*='user-menu']"
        login_indicator_fallback_2: "img[alt*='avatar']"
      notes: "Requires Anthropic account. Most stable UI."

    - name: gemini
      url: https://gemini.google.com
      enabled: true
      priority: 3
      selectors:
        chat_input_primary: "rich-textarea"
        chat_input_fallback_1: "textarea"
        chat_input_fallback_2: "[contenteditable='true']"
        submit_button_primary: "button[aria-label='Send message']"
        submit_button_fallback_1: "button[type='submit']"
        submit_button_fallback_2: "button:has-text('Submit')"
        response_container_primary: ".model-response-text"
        response_container_fallback_1: "[class*='response']"
        response_container_fallback_2: "[class*='message-content']"
        login_indicator_primary: "img[data-testid='user-avatar']"
        login_indicator_fallback_1: "[class*='user-avatar']"
        login_indicator_fallback_2: "img[alt*='Account']"
      notes: "Requires Google account. May have rate limiting."

  # Screenshot configuration
  screenshots:
    enabled: true
    format: png
    full_page: false
    on_success: true
    on_error: true
    naming_pattern: "screenshot-{llm}.png"

  # Output configuration
  output:
    file_pattern: "XX-llm-deep-research.md"
    include_timestamps: true
    include_screenshots: true
    include_synthesis: true

  # Error handling
  graceful_degradation:
    enabled: true
    description: "If one LLM fails, continue with others. Partial output is better than no output."
    min_successful_llms: 1

# Search wave configuration
search_waves:
  max_waves: 3
  coverage_threshold: 85       # target (APPROVE band starts here)
  min_coverage_to_proceed: 50  # below this after max waves = COVERAGE_GATE VETO
  review_band: [50, 70]        # REVIEW range — triggers P3.7 escape valve

# MCP tool dependencies
mcp_dependencies:
  playwright:
    tools:
      - mcp__playwright__browser_navigate
      - mcp__playwright__browser_click
      - mcp__playwright__browser_fill
      - mcp__playwright__browser_snapshot
      - mcp__playwright__browser_take_screenshot
      - mcp__playwright__browser_type
    required: false   # graceful degradation enabled
    fallback: "Skip Phase 3.7; document missing dependency in learning log; if --deep was explicit, escalate to user"
```


## Referência: references/squad/data/tech-research/auto-clarification.yaml

````yaml
auto_clarification:
  description: |
    Automatic context inference from the user query. Runs BEFORE the Strategic
    Brief Builder (Phase P1). Detects focus, domain, temporal intent, and
    product-validation intent. The inferred_context is a SEED for the brief —
    it NEVER skips clarification. The Strategic Brief Builder ALWAYS runs and
    turns the raw query into a structured, copy-pasteable Deep Research brief.
    This section is optional - if missing, the skill falls back to the legacy
    single-question clarification flow (backward compatible).

  patterns:
    technical:
      description: "Keywords indicating technical/code focus"
      keywords:
        - "codigo"
        - "código"
        - "implementar"
        - "implementação"
        - "how to"
        - "como implementar"
        - "como fazer"
        - "api"
        - "bug"
        - "error"
        - "erro"
        - "debug"
        - "code"
        - "implementation"
        - "library"
        - "biblioteca"
        - "sdk"
        - "tutorial"
        - "exemplo"
        - "example"
      inferred_value:
        focus: "technical"

    comparison:
      description: "Keywords indicating comparison focus"
      keywords:
        - "compare"
        - "comparar"
        - "vs"
        - "versus"
        - "diferenca"
        - "diferença"
        - "melhor"
        - "melhor entre"
        - "qual escolher"
        - "alternativa"
        - "alternative"
        - "tradeoff"
        - "pros and cons"
      inferred_value:
        focus: "comparison"

    recent:
      description: "Keywords indicating temporal/recency focus"
      keywords:
        - "latest"
        - "novo"
        - "nova"
        - "2024"
        - "2025"
        - "2026"
        - "atual"
        - "recente"
        - "recent"
        - "new"
        - "last year"
        - "estado da arte"
        - "state of the art"
        - "trending"
      inferred_value:
        temporal: "recent"
        search_constraint: "Append current year range to search queries for freshness"

    academic_signal:
      description: |
        Keywords indicating academic/scholarly research intent. Triggers adapter routing to
        scholarly databases (arXiv, PubMed, Semantic Scholar) before generic WebSearch in Phase 3.
        Added in v1.2.0 (2026-05-18) as part of STORY-154.2 scholarly adapter integration.
      keywords:
        - "arxiv"
        - "pubmed"
        - "paper"
        - "study"
        - "trial"
        - "cohort"
        - "systematic review"
        - "meta-analysis"
        - "peer-reviewed"
        - "systematic review"
        - "clinical trial"
        - "randomized controlled"
        - "academic"
        - "journal"
        - "doi"
        - "preprint"
        - "literature review"
      regex: "arxiv|pubmed|paper|study|trial|cohort|systematic review|meta-analysis|peer-reviewed"
      inferred_value:
        focus: "academic"
        adapter_routing: "scholarly_first"
        search_constraint: "Route to scholarly databases (arXiv/PubMed/Semantic Scholar) before generic WebSearch. Use scholarly_search.py bridge."

    product_validation:
      description: |
        Keywords indicating product idea validation. Triggers --product-discovery mode automatically.
        Added in v1.1.0 (2026-05-11) as bridge to spy:validate-product-idea molecule.
      keywords:
        - "validar ideia"
        - "validar produto"
        - "jtbd"
        - "jobs to be done"
        - "mom test"
        - "smoke test"
        - "willingness to pay"
        - "wtp"
        - "product-market fit"
        - "pmf"
        - "validate idea"
        - "validate product"
        - "lean startup"
        - "mvp validation"
        - "concierge mvp"
        - "blue ocean"
        - "founder-problem fit"
        - "early adopter"
        - "pre-sale"
        - "pré-venda"
      inferred_value:
        focus: "product-discovery"
        mode_flag: "--product-discovery"
        search_constraint: "Use Mom Test interview templates + villain mapping OSINT + blue ocean positioning frameworks instead of generic technical decomposition"
        cross_link:
          consumer: "spy:validate-product-idea"
          framework_ref: "squads/research/data/product-discovery-framework.md"

  technology_detection:
    description: |
      Common technologies to detect in queries. Case-insensitive matching.
      Handles variations (e.g., "node" matches "Node.js", "nodejs", "node.js").
      Detected technologies are set in inferred_context.domain as a list.
    technologies:
      languages:
        - { name: "JavaScript", aliases: ["javascript", "js", "ecmascript"] }
        - { name: "TypeScript", aliases: ["typescript", "ts"] }
        - { name: "Python", aliases: ["python", "py"] }
        - { name: "Java", aliases: ["java"] }
        - { name: "Go", aliases: ["go", "golang"] }
        - { name: "Rust", aliases: ["rust"] }
        - { name: "C#", aliases: ["c#", "csharp", "dotnet", ".net"] }
        - { name: "Ruby", aliases: ["ruby"] }
        - { name: "PHP", aliases: ["php"] }
        - { name: "Swift", aliases: ["swift"] }
        - { name: "Kotlin", aliases: ["kotlin"] }
      frameworks:
        - { name: "React", aliases: ["react", "reactjs", "react.js"] }
        - { name: "Next.js", aliases: ["next", "nextjs", "next.js"] }
        - { name: "Vue", aliases: ["vue", "vuejs", "vue.js"] }
        - { name: "Angular", aliases: ["angular"] }
        - { name: "Svelte", aliases: ["svelte", "sveltekit"] }
        - { name: "Express", aliases: ["express", "expressjs"] }
        - { name: "FastAPI", aliases: ["fastapi"] }
        - { name: "Django", aliases: ["django"] }
        - { name: "Flask", aliases: ["flask"] }
        - { name: "Spring", aliases: ["spring", "spring boot", "springboot"] }
        - { name: "Rails", aliases: ["rails", "ruby on rails"] }
        - { name: "Laravel", aliases: ["laravel"] }
      databases:
        - { name: "PostgreSQL", aliases: ["postgresql", "postgres", "pg"] }
        - { name: "MySQL", aliases: ["mysql"] }
        - { name: "MongoDB", aliases: ["mongodb", "mongo"] }
        - { name: "Redis", aliases: ["redis"] }
        - { name: "Memcached", aliases: ["memcached"] }
        - { name: "SQLite", aliases: ["sqlite"] }
        - { name: "Supabase", aliases: ["supabase"] }
        - { name: "Firebase", aliases: ["firebase", "firestore"] }
        - { name: "DynamoDB", aliases: ["dynamodb", "dynamo"] }
        - { name: "Elasticsearch", aliases: ["elasticsearch", "elastic"] }
      ai_ml:
        - { name: "LLM", aliases: ["llm", "llms", "large language model"] }
        - { name: "RAG", aliases: ["rag", "retrieval augmented generation"] }
        - { name: "LangChain", aliases: ["langchain"] }
        - { name: "OpenAI", aliases: ["openai", "gpt", "chatgpt"] }
        - { name: "Claude", aliases: ["claude", "anthropic"] }
        - { name: "TensorFlow", aliases: ["tensorflow", "tf"] }
        - { name: "PyTorch", aliases: ["pytorch", "torch"] }
        - { name: "Hugging Face", aliases: ["hugging face", "huggingface", "transformers"] }
      infra:
        - { name: "Docker", aliases: ["docker", "container", "containers"] }
        - { name: "Kubernetes", aliases: ["kubernetes", "k8s"] }
        - { name: "AWS", aliases: ["aws", "amazon web services"] }
        - { name: "Vercel", aliases: ["vercel"] }
        - { name: "Nginx", aliases: ["nginx"] }
        - { name: "GraphQL", aliases: ["graphql", "gql"] }
        - { name: "REST", aliases: ["rest", "restful", "rest api"] }
        - { name: "WebSocket", aliases: ["websocket", "ws", "websockets"] }

  strategic_brief_builder:
    description: |
      ALWAYS runs as Phase P1 (no skip path — replaces the legacy ask_threshold
      skip/1-question logic). Transforms the raw user query + inferred_context
      (seed) into a structured, copy-pasteable Deep Research brief, then asks
      2-3 clarifying questions OUTSIDE the code block so the operator can copy
      the brief even without answering.

    role: |
      You are a research-prompt strategist. You convert a simple question into a
      strategic Deep Research brief. EXPAND the scope, never narrow it. Bias
      toward actionable insight over generic summary. The brief is consumed
      internally by Phase P1.5 Decompose AND is copy-pasteable to an external
      Deep Research tool (OpenAI Deep Research, etc.).

    output_contract:
      format: |
        1. Emit the brief inside ONE fenced code block (```) so it is
           copy-pasteable AND machine-consumable by Phase P1.5.
        2. Emit the 2-3 clarifying questions AFTER and OUTSIDE the code block.
        3. NEVER put questions inside the code block.
        4. The brief must stand alone — answering the questions only refines it.
      language: |
        The BRIEF (everything inside the code block, including section headers)
        is ALWAYS in ENGLISH — it is pasted into Deep Research tools and drives
        English search queries (better coverage). The CLARIFYING QUESTIONS
        (outside the block) are in the operator's language (PT-BR default for
        AIOX operators).

    brief_structure:
      - id: TOPIC
        label: "TOPIC"
        instruction: "Reformulate into a strategic title; expand scope and add a time horizon when relevant."
      - id: CONTEXT
        label: "CONTEXT"
        instruction: "One short paragraph: purpose, practical objective, why this matters now."
      - id: SCOPE
        label: "SCOPE"
        instruction: |
          4-6 NAMED angles. For complex topics each angle SHOULD carry 2-4
          concrete sub-bullets (specific facets, not restatements). MUST cover:
          canonical definition / fundamentals; trends & case studies; relevant
          quantitative data; implementable aspects; risks & tradeoffs; relevant
          comparisons. Depth bar = the `few_shot_examples` design-system case
          (named angles in CAPS + nested sub-bullets). Each SCOPE angle becomes
          2-3 orthogonal sub-queries in Phase P1.5 — write them decomposable.
      - id: REQUIREMENTS
        label: "REQUIREMENTS"
        instruction: "3-4 parameters: recency vs historical baseline; geographic/demographic focus; technical depth vs accessibility; practical vs theoretical emphasis."
      - id: SOURCES
        label: "RECOMMENDED SOURCES"
        instruction: "3-4 specific source TYPES (not URLs) carrying the most evidential weight for this topic."
      - id: OUTCOMES
        label: "EXPECTED OUTCOMES"
        instruction: "3-5 concrete, applicable deliverables (frameworks, comparative matrices, roadmaps, model lists)."

    clarifying_questions:
      count: "2-3"
      placement: "outside_code_block"
      intent: "Sharpen scope / audience / the decision the research must inform. Skippable — the brief stands alone."

    seed_usage: |
      Use inferred_context to pre-fill the brief:
      - focus=technical    → bias SCOPE toward implementation + tradeoffs
      - focus=comparison   → SCOPE leads with a comparative-matrix angle
      - temporal=recent    → REQUIREMENTS demands current-year data; flag fast-moving area
      - domain=[techs]     → name them explicitly in TOPIC / SCOPE
      - product_discovery=true → reshape brief around JTBD, villain OSINT, WTP,
        blue ocean, validation case studies (see product-discovery-framework.md)

    template: |
      TOPIC: "{strategic title with expanded scope + time horizon}"

      CONTEXT: {one paragraph — purpose, practical objective, why now}

      SCOPE:
      1. {ANGLE NAME — canonical definition / fundamentals}:
         - {specific facet}
         - {specific facet}
      2. {ANGLE NAME — trends / case studies}:
         - {specific facet}
         - {specific facet}
      3. {ANGLE NAME — quantitative data}:
         - {specific facet}
      4. {ANGLE NAME — implementable aspects}:
         - {specific facet}
         - {specific facet}
      5. {ANGLE NAME — risks & tradeoffs}:
         - {specific facet}
      6. {ANGLE NAME — relevant comparison (optional, only if it adds signal)}:
         - {specific facet}

      REQUIREMENTS:
      - {recency vs historical baseline}
      - {geographic / demographic focus}
      - {technical depth vs accessibility}
      - {practical vs theoretical emphasis}

      RECOMMENDED SOURCES:
      - {source type 1}
      - {source type 2}
      - {source type 3}

      EXPECTED OUTCOMES:
      - {deliverable 1}
      - {deliverable 2}
      - {deliverable 3}

    few_shot_examples:
      calibration_note: |
        These are DEPTH ANCHORS, not formatting samples. Match this level:
        reframe the naive question into a strategic research TERRITORY, EXPAND
        scope, add a time horizon, make SCOPE angles specific (not "AI trends"
        but "growth in family-centered campaigns among Tier-1 brands, last 3
        years"). The brief (English, in a code block) and the questions
        (operator language, OUTSIDE the block).
      cases:
        - original: "Como ficar milionário usando a IA?"
          brief: |
            TOPIC: "Strategies for Building Millionaire-Level Wealth Using AI as Leverage (2025-2030)"

            CONTEXT: Understand how AI can be used as a multiplier of financial outcomes. Focus on evidence-based approaches to build substantial wealth over the next 5-10 years.

            SCOPE:
            1. PROVEN MODELS: Real cases of people/companies that reached 7-8 figure wealth with AI as the differentiator.
            2. PROMISING SECTORS: Niches with the best combination of high demand, high margins, and an AI-driven entry barrier.
            3. KEY COMPETENCIES: Skills most correlated with financial success in AI-based ventures.
            4. CAPITAL STRATEGIES: How resource-constrained founders have leveraged AI to fund expansion.
            5. RISKS & MITIGATIONS: Main failure factors and how to avoid them.
            6. EMERGING OPPORTUNITIES: 3-5 verticals with the highest potential over the next 36 months.

            REQUIREMENTS:
            - Concrete wealth-growth metrics
            - Strategies applicable by an individual / small team
            - Differentiate B2B, B2C, and B2B2C opportunities
            - Include specific "playbook" examples

            RECOMMENDED SOURCES:
            - Interviews with founders of successful AI startups
            - Venture capital reports (Sequoia, a16z, Y Combinator)
            - Sector analyses from consultancies (McKinsey, BCG)
            - Studies on predictive factors of success

            EXPECTED OUTCOMES:
            - 3-5 detailed business models with the highest potential
            - Framework for selecting high-potential opportunities
            - Roadmap for developing the required competencies
            - Comparative analysis across the different strategies
          clarifying_questions:
            - "Você quer foco em criar um negócio de IA ou em usar IA para alavancar um negócio existente?"
            - "Qual seu ponto de partida (capital, skill técnico, audiência)?"
            - "Horizonte: patrimônio em 5 anos agressivo ou 10 anos sustentável?"
        - original: "Como a causa família voltará como pauta nos próximos anos?"
          brief: |
            TOPIC: "Resurgence of Family as a Strategic Brand Territory: Trends and Opportunities (2025-2030)"

            CONTEXT: I identified a trend: global brands are pivoting toward family-centered messaging, possibly as a response to social fragmentation and anxiety about AI's impact.

            SCOPE:
            1. ENGAGEMENT DATA: Growth in family-centered campaigns among Tier-1 brands over the last 3 years.
            2. AI-VALUES CORRELATION: Relationship between AI adoption at work and shifts in family values.
            3. SECTOR ANALYSIS: Sectors leading vs. resisting this transition.
            4. DYNAMIC SPIRAL: Assess whether this is a "return movement" or an evolution toward new concepts.
            5. GLOBAL COMPARISON: Differences across North America, Europe, Asia, and Latin America.

            REQUIREMENTS:
            - Differentiate traditional vs. emerging definitions of "family"
            - Focus on psychographic over demographic analysis
            - Consider whether it is a cyclical phenomenon or a permanent shift

            RECOMMENDED SOURCES:
            - Marketing and consumer-behavior data
            - Opinions from CMOs and strategy directors
            - Social trend reports
            - Public-policy impact analyses

            EXPECTED OUTCOMES:
            - Quantitative evidence of a shift in brand positioning
            - Case studies of 3-5 successful campaigns
            - Strategic framework adaptable across industries
            - Forecast of evolution over the next 36 months
          clarifying_questions:
            - "Você quer ângulo de marca/marketing ou sociocultural amplo?"
            - "Mercado-alvo: global ou um recorte geográfico específico?"
            - "O output alimenta uma decisão de posicionamento de marca concreta?"
        - original: "Qual o melhor banco de dados vetorial?"
          brief: |
            TOPIC: "Vector Database Selection for Production RAG: Performance, Cost, and Operational Tradeoffs (2025-2026)"

            CONTEXT: I need to choose a vector store for a RAG pipeline going to production. I want a decision grounded in latency, total cost of ownership, and operational maturity — not vendor benchmark hype.

            SCOPE:
            1. REAL BENCHMARKS: p95/p99 latency and recall on datasets >10M vectors (pgvector, Pinecone, Qdrant, Weaviate, Milvus).
            2. TOTAL COST: Self-hosted vs managed, cost per million queries at scale, hidden operational cost.
            3. INTEGRATION & OPERATIONS: Metadata filtering, hybrid search, incremental index updates, maintenance effort.
            4. RISKS: Lock-in, scale limits, project maturity, documented production-failure post-mortems.
            5. DECISION COMPARISON: Decision matrix per scenario (early-stage startup vs enterprise vs edge/on-prem).

            REQUIREMENTS:
            - 2025-2026 data — discard pre-2024 benchmarks (fast-moving area)
            - Focus on production deployment, not prototyping
            - High technical depth — assume an engineer reader
            - Concrete numbers, not vendor marketing

            RECOMMENDED SOURCES:
            - Independent benchmarks (ANN-Benchmarks, academic papers)
            - Engineering blogs and post-mortems from companies in production
            - Official pricing and scale-limit documentation
            - Technical discussions (HN, eng forums) with real tradeoffs

            EXPECTED OUTCOMES:
            - Decision matrix per use scenario
            - Top 3 options with quantified cost/latency/maturity
            - Red-flag list per candidate
            - Grounded recommendation for "production RAG, 10M+ vectors"
          clarifying_questions:
            - "Qual a escala alvo (nº de vetores, QPS de pico)?"
            - "Self-hosted é requisito ou managed é aceitável?"
            - "Já tem Postgres na stack (pgvector reduz superfície operacional)?"
        - original: "Quais as melhores práticas de Design Atômico para design systems?"
          depth_tag: "GOLD — maximum-depth reference. Match THIS level for any non-trivial topic: named angles in CAPS, 2-4 nested sub-bullets each, 3-layer requirements (canonical / observed / operational), grouped source types, deliverables as concrete artifacts."
          brief: |
            TOPIC: "Operational Taxonomy of Atomic Design for Design Systems, UI Libraries, and Design-Test Artifacts in Complex Digital Products"

            CONTEXT: Investigate best practices for defining and applying Atomic Design in modern design systems, UI libraries, and visual documentation/testing tools. The goal is to separate Brad Frost's canonical definition from the operational adaptations used by mature product teams, especially in SaaS interfaces and digital products with complex shells, persistent navigation, composed layouts, and highly dynamic pages. The research must produce recommendations applicable to design-test artifacts for Medium, Gmail, and Amazon, with no code implementation.

            SCOPE:
            1. CANONICAL DEFINITION OF ATOMIC DESIGN:
               - Investigate Brad Frost's original definition of atoms, molecules, organisms, templates, and pages.
               - Identify the conceptual intent of each layer and the author's original examples.
               - Clearly separate the original definition from later interpretations.
            2. ADAPTATION FOR SAAS PRODUCTS AND COMPLEX INTERFACES:
               - Differentiate organisms, templates, and pages in products with application shells, sidebars, persistent headers, dashboards, grids, feeds, inboxes, and authenticated flows.
               - Assess when a shell should be classified as an organism, template, layout pattern, or page structure.
               - Consider dynamic, personalized, responsive, or multi-state composed pages.
            3. MATURE DESIGN SYSTEMS:
               - Compare how Material Design, Carbon, Polaris, Atlassian, Fluent, GOV.UK, and Lightning define foundations, components, patterns, layouts, templates, and page-level experiences.
               - Identify convergences and divergences relative to classic Atomic Design.
            4. UI AND DOCUMENTATION TOOLING:
               - Investigate how Storybook, Chromatic, and visual-testing platforms treat small components, composed components, patterns, layouts, and pages.
               - Assess organization of hierarchies, stories, args, states, variants, and page-level examples.
               - Identify naming, grouping, and granularity practices.
            5. TAXONOMY FOR DESIGN-TESTS:
               - Propose an operational taxonomy applicable to Medium, Gmail, and Amazon.
               - Differentiate foundation, primitive, atom, molecule, component, organism, pattern, layout/template, page, and flow.
               - Consider feed, inbox, search, PDP, cart, checkout, global navigation, and dashboards.
            6. RISKS, TRADE-OFFS, AND OPERATIONAL DECISIONS:
               - Map the risks of overly theoretical, ambiguous, or hard-to-maintain taxonomies.
               - Weigh trade-offs between fidelity to original Atomic Design and practical usability for design, eng, and visual QA.
               - Identify objective criteria for ambiguous cases.

            REQUIREMENTS:
            1. Prioritize primary sources: Brad Frost (book/articles), official design-system docs, official UI/component-testing tool docs.
            2. Separate three analysis layers: canonical definition; observed adaptation; operational recommendation.
            3. Keep a practical focus: applicable recommendations, no code, with concrete examples from Medium, Gmail, and Amazon.
            4. Balance conceptual precision and utility: do not treat Atomic Design as a rigid rule; state explicitly when a recommendation is a pragmatic adaptation, not the original definition.

            RECOMMENDED SOURCES:
            1. Atomic Design primary sources: Brad Frost's book, site, articles, and talks.
            2. Official design-system docs: Material, Carbon, Polaris, Atlassian, Fluent, GOV.UK, Lightning.
            3. Official tool docs: Storybook, Chromatic, Playwright CT, Testing Library, Figma component docs.
            4. Studies and practice guides: design-systems, frontend, design-ops, visual regression testing, component-driven UI teams.

            EXPECTED OUTCOMES:
            1. Comparative table of Brad Frost's canonical definition of atoms/molecules/organisms/templates/pages.
            2. Operational adaptation map: foundations/components/patterns/templates/layouts/pages/flows across mature design systems.
            3. Decision guide for ambiguous cases: objective criteria for organisms vs templates vs pages in complex shells.
            4. Recommended design-test taxonomy: categories, inclusion criteria, examples and anti-examples (Medium/Gmail/Amazon).
            5. Practical recommendations: naming, organization, documentation; how to avoid overlap; design/eng/QA alignment.
            6. Executive synthesis: conclusions, trade-offs, final taxonomy recommendation for immediate adoption.
          clarifying_questions:
            - "A taxonomia final é para um design system próprio ou para auditar/classificar interfaces de terceiros (Medium/Gmail/Amazon)?"
            - "O consumidor é design, engenharia ou QA visual — ou os três precisam de uma única taxonomia compartilhada?"
            - "Stack de documentação alvo é Storybook, ou precisa ser tool-agnostic?"

    decomposition_contract: |
      The strategic_brief is the input to Phase P1.5 Decompose. Decomposition is
      NOT capped at 5-7 for rich briefs: generate 2-3 orthogonal sub-queries PER
      SCOPE angle (and its sub-bullets), honoring REQUIREMENTS as search
      constraints. Floor 5 (thin briefs), ceiling ~18 (M4 runs a search wave per
      sub-query — cost is linear). A 6-angle GOLD-depth brief → ~12-18 queries.
      product-discovery mode keeps its fixed 5-7 framework (JTBD/Villain/WTP/
      BlueOcean/CaseStudies + 2 optional) — it does NOT scale.

    legacy_single_question_fallback: |
      Used ONLY if strategic_brief_builder cannot run (config error). Ask one
      combined question: "Sua query parece ampla. Em uma frase: qual o foco e
      contexto desta pesquisa?"
````

```yaml
commands:
  - "'*help' - Show available commands"
  - "'*research {query}' - Start full research pipeline"
  - "'*quick {query}' - Fast research (skip clarification)"
  - "'*status' - Show current research status"
  - "'*exit' - Exit skill"

flags:
  - flag: "--product-discovery"
    alias: "--pd"
    description: "Product discovery mode — injects PD-specific sub-queries (JTBD framing, villain root cause, WTP signals, blue ocean, hypothesis structuring) into decompose phase. Feeds spy:validate-product-idea molecule."
    added_in: "1.1.0"
    behavior: |
      When set, Phase 1.5 (Decompose) uses the product-discovery sub-query template
      instead of the technical decomposition. Phase 2 (Generate Prompt) embeds the
      JTBD canonical format and villain-mapping evidence schema in the research
      prompt. Phase 5 (Document) adds an optional `06-product-discovery-validation.md`
      section with GO/NO-GO score against `spy/checklists/product-discovery-gates.yaml`.
    cross_link:
      consumer: "spy:validate-product-idea (Wave 0 molecule)"
      framework: "squads/research/data/product-discovery-framework.md"
  - flag: "--deep"
    description: "Force multi-LLM Playwright deep-research phase (Grok/Claude/Gemini)"
    note: "Existing flag — documented here for completeness"
```


## Referência: references/squad/data/tech-research/dependencies.yaml

```yaml
dependencies:
  templates:
    - deep-research-prompt-template.md
    - output-structure.md
  prompts:
    - decompose.md
    - evaluate.md
    - page-extract.md
    - tech-discovery.md
    - verify-citations.md
    - tool-strategy.md       # Exa/Context7/ETL/WebSearch hierarchy with fallbacks
    - executor-matrix.md     # Worker vs Agent classification (deterministic vs LLM)
    - playwright-deep-research.md  # NEW: Multi-LLM browser automation workflow
  config:
    - config.yaml            # NEW: Playwright deep research configuration

  infrastructure:
    etl_service: "services/etl/"
    etl_youtube_cli: "node services/etl/bin/youtube-transcript.js {videoId}"
    etl_blog_cli: "node services/etl/bin/fetch-page.js {url}"
    etl_blog_api: "ETLService.collectBlog(url)"

  worker_scripts:
    base_path: "squads/research/scripts/tech-research/"
    scripts:
      - id: scaffold
        path: "squads/research/scripts/tech-research/scaffold.py"
        atoms: [atm_scaffold_output]
        cli: "python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/scaffold.py --slug {slug} --title \"{title}\" --query \"{query}\" --date {YYYY-MM-DD}"
        stdin: "echo '{\"slug\":\"...\",\"title\":\"...\",\"query\":\"...\"}' | python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/scaffold.py --stdin"
        behavior: "Creates folder + 4 stub files (README, 00, 02, 03) with correct templates. Idempotent — never overwrites existing files."
      - id: url_detector
        path: "squads/research/scripts/tech-research/url_detector.py"
        atoms: [atm_classify_urls, atm_parse_query]
        cli: "python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/url_detector.py {url}"
        batch: "echo '[\"url1\",\"url2\"]' | python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/url_detector.py --stdin"
      - id: credibility_scorer
        path: "squads/research/scripts/tech-research/credibility_scorer.py"
        atoms: [atm_pattern_match]
        cli: "python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/credibility_scorer.py {url}"
        batch: "echo '[{\"url\":\"...\",\"title\":\"...\"}]' | python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/credibility_scorer.py --stdin"
      - id: coverage_calculator
        path: "squads/research/scripts/tech-research/coverage_calculator.py"
        atoms: [atm_calc_coverage, atm_calc_newinfo, atm_stopping_decision]
        cli_coverage: "echo '{dimensions_json}' | python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/coverage_calculator.py coverage"
        cli_newinfo: "python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/coverage_calculator.py newinfo --new {N} --total {M}"
        cli_stop: "echo '{state_json}' | python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/coverage_calculator.py stop"
      - id: metrics_collector
        path: "squads/research/scripts/tech-research/metrics_collector.py"
        atoms: [atm_compute_metrics, atm_save_state]
        cli_compute: "echo '{data_json}' | python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/metrics_collector.py compute"
        cli_save: "echo '{state_json}' | python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/metrics_collector.py save --dir {output_dir}"
      - id: logger
        path: "squads/research/scripts/tech-research/logger.py"
        atoms: [all_worker_atoms]
        cli: "python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/logger.py {atom_id} {level} {event} '{data_json}'"
        python: "from infrastructure.services.tech_research.logger import ResearchLogger"
      - id: output_validator
        path: "squads/research/scripts/tech-research/output_validator.py"
        atoms: [QG-PROD-6]
        cli: "python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/output_validator.py {output_dir}"
      - id: claim_extractor
        path: "squads/research/scripts/tech-research/claim_extractor.py"
        atoms: [atm_extract_claims, atm_match_sources]
        cli_extract: "python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/claim_extractor.py extract < {report.md}"
        cli_match: "echo '{claims_and_sources_json}' | python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/claim_extractor.py match"
      - id: research_graph
        path: "squads/research/scripts/tech-research/research_graph.py"
        atoms: [atm_build_graph]
        cli: "python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/research_graph.py {output_dir}"
        check: "python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/research_graph.py {output_dir} --check"
        behavior: |
          Derives research-graph.json from filesystem (node types: root/query/prompt/report/
          recommendations/followup/wave/quick_wins/evolving/curiosity/log/metrics/pipeline_state;
          edge relations: contains/produces/spawns_followup/checkpoint/derives/describes).
          Inspired by btahir/open-deep-research "Flow" / Visual Research Mapping. Zero LLM, zero
          network, deterministic. Run as last step of Phase 5 (after metrics_collector save).
      - id: research_kb_index
        path: "squads/research/scripts/tech-research/research_kb_index.py"
        atoms: [atm_index_kb]
        cli: "python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/research_kb_index.py --root docs/research"
        check: "python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/research_kb_index.py --root docs/research --check"
        behavior: |
          Scans docs/research/* and emits docs/research/_index.json with cross-research catalog
          (slug, topic, date, coverage_score, sources, decision, status, tags). Knowledge-Base
          pattern from btahir/open-deep-research (filesystem-backed instead of localStorage).
          Fallback chain (QF-3.1): canonical YAML/README → folder-name date → filesystem mtime
          → first '#' heading → URL counting in references. Each field carries an `inferred`
          flag so downstream consumers know what came from canonical vs heuristic source.
          Idempotent — run after every Phase 5 completion to keep the index fresh.
      - id: sources_extractor
        path: "squads/research/scripts/tech-research/sources_extractor.py"
        atoms: [atm_extract_sources]
        cli: "python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/sources_extractor.py {output_dir}"
        check: "python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/sources_extractor.py {output_dir} --check"
        behavior: |
          Parses 02-research-report.md and any followup files in the same research folder,
          emitting {output_dir}/sources.yaml — an artifact-first source manifest with
          id, url, title, date (inline annotation or 'date_unknown'), credibility
          (delegated to credibility_scorer.py), first_seen_in (filename), first_seen_section
          (nearest markdown heading), kind (markdown_link|bare_url), and totals.
          QF-4 from btahir parity quick-fix set; consumer for verify-citations + Observatory
          "Source evidence drawer" pattern. Dedup is per-URL keeping the earliest occurrence.
          Idempotent, atomic write, zero LLM, zero network.
      - id: players_extractor
        path: "squads/research/scripts/tech-research/players_extractor.py"
        atoms: [atm_extract_players]
        cli: "python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/players_extractor.py {output_dir}"
        check: "python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/players_extractor.py {output_dir} --check"
        behavior: |
          QF-D1. Parses `### N.N Name` deep-dive blocks (matching the canonical
          "DEEP DIVES ON TOP PLAYERS" template enforced by phase-5-document.yaml)
          into players.yaml with what_it_does, what_it_does_not, insight, source
          (title+url+date+optional additional sources), tier, category, role, fit,
          action, and excluded flag (scans narrative for EXCLUÍDO/EXCLUDED tokens).
          Explicit deep-dive fields are authoritative; heuristic fallback is only
          used when a legacy report lacks those fields. Idempotent; zero LLM; zero network.
      - id: comparison_matrix_extractor
        path: "squads/research/scripts/tech-research/comparison_matrix_extractor.py"
        atoms: [atm_extract_matrices]
        cli: "python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/comparison_matrix_extractor.py {output_dir}"
        check: "python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/comparison_matrix_extractor.py {output_dir} --check"
        behavior: |
          QF-D2. Every markdown table sitting under a `## N. ...` heading becomes a
          structured matrix entry in matrices.yaml (columns + cells as {col: value}).
          Tables inside `### N.N` player blocks are ignored (those belong to players.yaml).
          Unlocks sortable/filterable comparison UI in the Observatory without parsing
          markdown at view time. Idempotent; zero LLM; zero network.
      - id: ux_patterns_extractor
        path: "squads/research/scripts/tech-research/ux_patterns_extractor.py"
        atoms: [atm_extract_patterns]
        cli: "python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/ux_patterns_extractor.py {output_dir}"
        check: "python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/ux_patterns_extractor.py {output_dir} --check"
        behavior: |
          QF-D3. Scans `##` sections whose title matches /padr(ões|ão|ao)|pattern/i
          and parses numbered bold items (`N. **Name:** Description`) into a UX
          patterns catalog (id, number, name, description, reference, section).
          Cross-research aggregate `docs/research/_ux-patterns.json` is a separate
          future enhancement (tracked in curiosity_queue). Idempotent; zero LLM;
          zero network.

  mcp_servers:
    context7:
      tools: ["mcp__context7__resolve-library-id", "mcp__context7__query-docs"]
      fallback: "WebSearch with site:{library}.dev"
    exa:
      tools: ["mcp__exa__web_search_exa", "mcp__exa__research_paper_search", "mcp__exa__github_search", "mcp__exa__crawling"]
      fallback: "WebSearch (native)"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # rate_limits — adopted from btahir/open-deep-research lib/config.ts pattern
  # (docs/research/2026-05-11-visual-deep-research-apps/02-research-report.md §1.1)
  # Advisory in this skill: the orchestrator reads these knobs to pace tool
  # dispatch within a phase. There is no enforcement daemon; on_breach controls
  # behavior when the budget is exceeded during a wave.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  rate_limits:
    enabled: true
    search_per_minute: 10           # WebSearch + Exa + Context7 search combined
    content_fetch_per_minute: 20    # WebFetch + ETL fetch-page + curl downloads
    synthesis_per_minute: 5         # Phase 4 LLM-heavy synthesis calls
    deep_read_per_minute: 6         # Phase 3.2 page-extract WebFetch budget
    on_breach: log_warning_continue # log_warning_continue | sleep_until_window | abort_wave
    window_seconds: 60
    burst_factor: 1.5               # short-lived bursts allowed up to 1.5x rate
    notes:
      - "Workers (Python scripts under squads/research/scripts/tech-research/) are exempt: zero network."
      - "Multi-LLM (Phase 3.7 Playwright) is also exempt: browser automation pacing is handled by playwright config.yaml."
      - "When on_breach=log_warning_continue (default), the orchestrator emits a structured log line via scripts/logger.py and proceeds."
```

```yaml
# Token Registry — Research Squad
# 12 SINKRA tokens across 9 families governing benchmark and research
# Version: 2.0.0 (enriched per sinkra-upgrade-squad)

time:
  - benchmark_window
capacity:
  - max_parallel_subjects
threshold:
  - benchmark_quality_gate
  - report_release_gate
priority:
  - subject_priority
permission:
  - source_access_scope
taxonomy:
  - comparison_type
behavior:
  - fail_loud_publish
  - benchmark_evidence_pack
accountability:
  - spy_operator_approval
mode:
  - ENTENDER
  - EXPLORAR
  - VALIDAR

tokens:
  - token_name: benchmark_window
    family: Time
    semantic: "Janela temporal usada para recorte de evidências"
    sinkra_refs:
      - composition_mapping.atoms.tasks/bench-detect.md
      - composition_mapping.molecules.mol-benchmark-core
    default_value: "30d"
    enforcement: advisory
    version: "1.0.0"
    produces_by: [bench-detect]
    consumes_by: [bench-score, bench-gap]

  - token_name: max_parallel_subjects
    family: Capacity
    semantic: "Número máximo de sujeitos processados em paralelo"
    sinkra_refs:
      - composition_mapping.atoms.tasks/bench-inventory.md
    default_value: 2
    enforcement: strict
    version: "1.0.0"
    produces_by: [bench-detect]
    consumes_by: [bench-inventory, bench-matrix]

  - token_name: benchmark_quality_gate
    family: Threshold
    semantic: "Threshold principal para benchmark aprovado"
    sinkra_refs:
      - workflows/bench-comparison-pipeline.yaml → phase 9 scoring.pass_threshold
      - checklists/bench-quality-checklist.md → scoring
    default_value: 0.9
    enforcement: veto
    version: "1.0.0"
    produces_by: [bench-score]
    consumes_by: [bench-report, bench-battle-card]

  - token_name: subject_priority
    family: Priority
    semantic: "Prioridade relativa entre subjects e fontes"
    sinkra_refs:
      - composition_mapping.atoms.tasks/bench-detect.md
    default_value: "equal"
    enforcement: advisory
    version: "1.0.0"
    produces_by: [bench-detect]
    consumes_by: [bench-inventory]

  - token_name: source_access_scope
    family: Permission
    semantic: "Escopo permitido de acesso a dados e repositórios"
    sinkra_refs:
      - data/capability-tools.yaml
      - data/bench-data-sources.yaml
    default_value: "public"
    enforcement: strict
    version: "1.0.0"
    produces_by: [bench-detect]
    consumes_by: [bench-codebase-recon, bench-inventory]

  - token_name: comparison_type
    family: Taxonomy
    semantic: "Tipo canônico de comparação benchmark"
    sinkra_refs:
      - composition_mapping.atoms.tasks/bench-detect.md
      - workflows/bench-comparison-pipeline.yaml → type_routing
    default_value: "auto"
    enforcement: strict
    version: "1.0.0"
    produces_by: [bench-detect]
    consumes_by: [bench-inventory, bench-matrix, bench-score, bench-gap, bench-deep-compare]

  - token_name: fail_loud_publish
    family: Behavior
    semantic: "Comportamento de falha explícita na publicação"
    sinkra_refs:
      - config.yaml → logging.error_behavior
    default_value: true
    enforcement: strict
    version: "1.0.0"
    produces_by: [config]
    consumes_by: [bench-report-publish]

  - token_name: spy_operator_approval
    family: Accountability
    semantic: "Aprovação humana obrigatória para publicação crítica"
    sinkra_refs:
      - agents/research-operator.md
      - data/quality-gates.yaml → governance
    default_value: true
    enforcement: veto
    version: "1.0.0"
    produces_by: [research-operator]
    consumes_by: [bench-report, bench-battle-card]

  - token_name: ENTENDER
    family: Mode
    semantic: "Modo de entendimento profundo"
    sinkra_refs:
      - config.yaml → supported_modes
    default_value: null
    enforcement: advisory
    version: "1.0.0"
    produces_by: [config]
    consumes_by: [deep-research-collect, deep-research-patterns]

  - token_name: EXPLORAR
    family: Mode
    semantic: "Modo de exploração comparativa"
    sinkra_refs:
      - config.yaml → supported_modes
      - workflows/bench-comparison-pipeline.yaml
    default_value: null
    enforcement: advisory
    version: "1.0.0"
    produces_by: [config]
    consumes_by: [bench-detect, bench-matrix, bench-score]

  - token_name: VALIDAR
    family: Mode
    semantic: "Modo de validação rigorosa e quality gate"
    sinkra_refs:
      - config.yaml → supported_modes
      - workflows/bench-comparison-pipeline.yaml → phase 9
    default_value: null
    enforcement: advisory
    version: "1.0.0"
    produces_by: [config]
    consumes_by: [bench-traceability, bench-battle-card, bench-report]

  - token_name: benchmark_evidence_pack
    family: Behavior

## 1. TITLE FORMULAS (Proven)

```
"You've Been [Doing X] the WRONG WAY (do this instead)"
"You've Been Using [X] the Hard Way (Use This Instead)"

### 1.2 Urgency + FOMO
```
"You NEED to learn [X] NOW!!"
"[X] will change EVERYTHING (and you're missing out)"
```
**Performance:** 1.2M views (NetworkChuck)

### 1.3 Number + Value Compression
```
"[X] hours of study in [Y] minutes"

"Learn [X] in [impossible time]"
```
**Performance:** 431K-797K views

## Referência: references/squad/docs/tech-research-README.md

# Tech Research v3.2 - Deep Technical Research Pipeline

**Version:** 3.2
**Last Updated:** 2026-05-06
**Epic:** TECH-RESEARCH-001
**Skill Path:** `.claude/skills/tech-research/`

---

## Overview

Tech Research is an AIOX skill that transforms technical questions into structured, documented research with actionable findings. It automates the full pipeline: query analysis, multi-source search, coverage evaluation, and synthesis.

### What Changed from v3.1

| Aspect | v3.1 declared | v3.2 current |
|--------|----|----|
| Search execution | Orchestrator-Worker (Haiku subagents) | Main-context Agent default; optional worker only if runtime exposes it |
| Model routing | Haiku for search/read/eval, Main for synthesis | Main runtime with deterministic scripts for scoring, metrics, validation |
| Mechanical artifacts | Optional/recommended in practice | `metrics.yaml` and `pipeline-state.yaml` mandatory |
| Completion gate | Validator advisory | `output_validator.py` blocks completion |
| Version traceability | No explicit marker | `workflow_version` required in SKILL, README metadata, metrics |

### What Changed from v1

| Aspect | v1 | v2 |
|--------|----|----|
| Clarification | 3 fixed questions (always) | Auto-inference, 0-1 questions |
| Search | Sequential, single thread | Parallel dispatch, multi-query |
| Depth Control | None (subjective) | Coverage evaluation loop with thresholds |
| Cost Control | None (unbounded) | Token budgets per phase via config.yaml |
| Configuration | Hardcoded | External config.yaml, fully tunable |

### Key Features

- **Auto-Clarification**: Pattern matching + technology detection infers context automatically
- **Query Decomposition**: Breaks query into 3-7 atomic, searchable sub-queries
- **Runtime-Honest Search**: Executes sub-queries in main context unless an actual worker exists
- **Coverage Evaluation Loop**: Iterates search waves until coverage >= 80% or diminishing returns
- **Mechanical Traceability**: Requires metrics, pipeline state, workflow version, citation marker, and validator pass
- **Backward Compatible**: Every v2 feature degrades gracefully if its dependency is missing

---

## Architecture

### Pipeline Phases (v3.2 - Runtime-Honest Agent + Mandatory Gates)

```
Query recebida
    |
    v
[Phase -1: Load Config]
    |
    v
[Phase 0: Auto-Clarify] (MAIN MODEL, inline)
    |
    +- Detects patterns + technologies
    |
    v
[Phase 1.5: Decompose] (MAIN MODEL, ultrathink)
    |
    +- Produces 5-7 sub-queries
    |
    v
[Phase 2: Generate Prompt] (MAIN MODEL)
    |
    v
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
|  RESEARCH LOOP (max 3 waves)                              |
|                                                           |
|  [Phase 3: Execute Sub-queries] (MAIN MODEL default)      |
|      +- Optional deep-researcher only if runtime exposes it |
|      +- Writes wave-N-progress.jsonl after each sub-query |
|      +- Recovers from timeout by reading progress JSONL   |
|      |                                                    |
|      v                                                    |
|  [Phase 3.2: Deep Read] (MAIN MODEL + ETL/scripts)        |
|      +- YouTube -> ETL CLI (always)                       |
|      +- Blogs -> ETL fetch-page CLI (primary)             |
|      +- Other -> WebFetch (fallback)                      |
|      |                                                    |
|      v                                                    |
|  [Phase 3.5: Evaluate Coverage] (script-assisted)         |
|      +- coverage >= 80%?    -> STOP                       |
|      +- new_info < 0.1?     -> STOP                       |
|      +- iteration >= max?   -> FORCE STOP                 |
|      +- else                -> CONTINUE (next wave)       |
|      |                                                    |
|      v                                                    |
|  [Phase 3.6: Compress Wave] (structured summary)          |
|      +- Compresses wave results into concise summary      |
|      +- Saves wave-N-summary.md to output dir             |
|      +- Next wave reads summaries, not raw data           |
+-----------------------------------------------------------+
    |
    v
[Phase 4: Synthesize] (MAIN MODEL) ← reads wave-*-summary.md
    |
    v
[Phase 4.5: Verify Citations] (MAIN MODEL)
    |
    v
[Phase 5: Document] (MAIN MODEL) -> docs/research/{date}-{slug}/
    |
    +- metrics.yaml + pipeline-state.yaml mandatory
    +- output_validator.py must pass before completion
```

### Model Routing

| Phase | Model | Why |
|-------|-------|-----|
| 0, 1, 1.5, 2 | Main (Opus/Sonnet) | Planning requires deep reasoning |
| 3, 3.2, 3.5, 3.6 | Main + deterministic scripts | Current runtime evidence shows worker dispatch is not reliable |
| 4, 4.5, 5 | Main (Opus/Sonnet) | Synthesis requires judgment and creativity |

### Cost Expectations

Cost is measured from runtime artifacts, not promised from an aspirational routing plan.
`metrics.yaml` is the source of truth for wave count, tool count, model tier, and validator result.

### ETL Integration

The skill uses the ETL service at `services/etl/` for zero-cost content extraction:

**YouTube Transcripts:**
```bash
node services/etl/bin/youtube-transcript.js {videoId} --format json
```

**Blog/Article Extraction (PRIMARY for blog domains):**
```bash
node services/etl/bin/fetch-page.js {url}
# Exit 0 = success, 1 = blocked domain (skip), 2-4 = try WebFetch fallback
```

**Supported Blog Domains (ETL primary):**
dev.to, medium.com, marktechpost.com, hashnode.dev, hackernoon.com, freecodecamp.org/news, blog.*, *.blog.*

---

## File Structure

```
.claude/skills/tech-research/
+-- SKILL.md                     # Main workflow definition (v3, ~1000 lines)
+-- config.yaml                  # Token budgets + iteration params
+-- README.md                    # This file
+-- prompts/
|   +-- decompose.md             # Query decomposition prompt (Phase 1.5)
|   +-- evaluate.md              # Coverage evaluation prompt (Phase 3.5)
|   +-- page-extract.md          # Deep page content extraction
|   +-- tech-discovery.md        # Tool/MCP/API discovery
|   +-- verify-citations.md      # Citation integrity verification
|   +-- tool-strategy.md         # Tool hierarchy + fallback chains (v3 ETL-first)
|   +-- executor-matrix.md       # Worker vs Agent + Model Tier classification
+-- templates/
    +-- deep-research-prompt-template.md  # Research prompt template (Phase 2)
    +-- output-structure.md              # Output format reference
```

---

## Quick Start

```
/tech-research "como implementar rate limiting em Node.js"
```

The skill will:
1. Auto-detect focus (technical) and domain (Node.js) -- skip clarification
2. Decompose into sub-queries (definitions, libraries, examples, benchmarks)
3. Search all sub-queries in parallel
4. Evaluate coverage, iterate if needed
5. Synthesize findings into a structured report
6. Save to `docs/research/2026-02-07-rate-limiting-nodejs/`

---

## Usage Guide

### Basic Usage

```
/tech-research "your technical question here"
```

The skill accepts any technical question in Portuguese or English.

### Auto-Clarification Behavior

The skill analyzes your query before asking questions:

- **Query contains technical keywords** (code, api, implementation, etc.) or **known technologies** (React, PostgreSQL, Docker, etc.): Proceeds directly with 0 questions.
- **Query is ambiguous** (e.g., "pesquise sobre performance"): Asks 1 combined clarification question.
- **auto_clarification section missing from SKILL.md** (backward compat): Falls back to original 3-question flow.

### Tuning Token Budgets

Edit `.claude/skills/tech-research/config.yaml`:

```yaml
tokens:
  decomposition_output: 500    # Max tokens for query decomposition output
  source_content_max: 1000     # Max tokens per individual source (truncates longer)
  synthesis_input_max: 5000    # Max total tokens fed to synthesis phase
  final_report_max: 2000       # Soft limit for final report output
```

- **Lower values** = cheaper, faster, more concise reports
- **Higher values** = more thorough but more expensive
- All budgets use soft limits (prompt instructions) except source_content_max (hard truncation)

### Tuning Iteration Parameters

```yaml
iteration:
  max_iterations: 3            # Hard cap on search waves (1 = single wave, no iteration)
  coverage_threshold: 0.8      # Stop when coverage >= 80% (range: 0.0-1.0)
  min_new_info_ratio: 0.1      # Stop when new info < 10% (diminishing returns)
```

- **max_iterations: 1** = disable iteration loop (single search wave, like v1)
- **coverage_threshold: 0.9** = higher quality bar, more iterations
- **min_new_info_ratio: 0.05** = tolerate more diminishing returns before stopping

### Expected Output Structure

```
docs/research/{YYYY-MM-DD}-{slug}/
+-- README.md                    # Index + TL;DR
+-- 00-query-original.md         # Original question + context
+-- 01-deep-research-prompt.md   # Generated research prompt
+-- 02-research-report.md        # Complete findings + Coverage Evaluation Summary
+-- 03-recommendations.md        # Recommendations and next steps
+-- metrics.yaml                 # Mandatory run metrics
+-- pipeline-state.yaml          # Mandatory run state
```

### Troubleshooting

| Issue | Cause | Fix |
|-------|-------|-----|
| Skill asks 3 questions instead of 0-1 | `auto_clarification` section missing or malformed | Verify SKILL.md YAML block is valid |
| Single search wave (no iteration) | `prompts/evaluate.md` missing | Restore file from skill directory |
| No query decomposition | `prompts/decompose.md` missing | Restore file from skill directory |
| config.yaml parse error in logs | Invalid YAML syntax | Validate YAML (check indentation, colons) |
| Sources marked [TRUNCATED] | Source exceeded `source_content_max` budget | Normal behavior; increase budget if needed |

---

## Configuration Reference

### config.yaml

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `tokens.decomposition_output` | int | 500 | Max tokens for Phase 1.5 decomposition output |
| `tokens.source_content_max` | int | 1000 | Max tokens per source; hard truncation with [TRUNCATED] marker |
| `tokens.synthesis_input_max` | int | 5000 | Max total tokens fed to Phase 4 synthesis; lowest-priority sources dropped |
| `tokens.final_report_max` | int | 2000 | Soft limit for final report output (via prompt instruction) |
| `iteration.max_iterations` | int | 3 | Hard cap on search waves; FORCE STOP at this count |
| `iteration.coverage_threshold` | float | 0.8 | Stop when coverage_score >= threshold * 100 |
| `iteration.min_new_info_ratio` | float | 0.1 | Stop when new_info_ratio < this value (2nd+ iteration only) |

All values have built-in defaults in SKILL.md. If config.yaml is missing or fails to parse, defaults are used automatically.

---

## Metrics: v1 vs v2

### v1 Baseline (measured, Story 0.1)

| Query | Type | Tokens | Time | Cost (Sonnet) | Quality |
|-------|------|--------|------|---------------|---------|
| Q1: "o que e RAG?" | Simple | 70,944 | 3m 38s | $0.21 | 4/5 |
| Q2: "rate limiting Node.js" | Technical | 67,012 | 2m 59s | $0.20 | 4/5 |
| Q4: "deep research LLMs" | Deep | 88,543 | 4m 40s | $0.27 | 5/5 |
| **Average** | - | **75,500** | **3m 46s** | **$0.40*** | **4.3/5** |

*Cost recalculated with 80/20 input/output split

### v2 Feature-by-Feature Impact (expected)

| Metric | v1 Baseline | v2 Feature | Expected Impact | Status |
|--------|-------------|------------|-----------------|--------|
| Questions asked | 3 (always) | Auto-clarification | 0-1 questions | Implemented |
| Search approach | Sequential | Parallel dispatch | -50% time | Implemented |
| Cost control | None | Token budgets | Predictable cost | Implemented |
| Search depth | Single wave | Iteration loop | Adaptive depth | Implemented |
| Config | Hardcoded | config.yaml | Tunable | Implemented |
| Average cost | $0.40 | Target: $0.20 | -50% | Needs validation |
| Average time | 3m 46s | Target: 1m 53s | -50% | Needs validation |
| Quality | 4.3/5 | Target: >=3.9/5 | >=90% maintained | Needs validation |

**Note:** Quantitative v2 metrics (cost, time, quality) are projections based on implemented features. Actual measurements require a validation run with the 5 baseline queries.

### What Was Validated vs What Needs Manual Validation

**Validated (implemented and verified):**
- Auto-clarification: pattern matching and technology detection working
- Query decomposition: decompose.md produces 3-7 sub-queries
- Parallel search: WebSearch calls dispatched simultaneously
- Stopping criteria: coverage evaluation loop with configurable thresholds
- Token budgets: config.yaml loaded and enforced across all phases

**Needs manual validation run:**
- Average cost reduction >= 50% (requires executing 5 test queries)
- Average time reduction >= 50% (requires timed execution)
- Quality maintained >= 90% of baseline (requires subjective evaluation)

---

## Backward Compatibility

Every v3 feature has an explicit fallback to v2 behavior:

| Feature | Fallback | Trigger |
|---------|----------|---------|
| ETL for blogs | WebFetch (v2 behavior) | ETL service unavailable or fetch-page.js fails with exit code 2-4 |
| Optional worker routing | Main model execution | Runtime does not expose a real `deep-researcher` worker |
| Subagent parallelism | Sequential execution | Task tool dispatch fails for any subagent |
| ETL for YouTube | No fallback (ETL has 100% success rate) | Should not fail |

---

# Tool Discovery Report - Research Squad

## Metadata
- Date: 2026-02-17
- Squad: `spy`
- Domain: Competitive intelligence (YouTube + Instagram) and framework benchmarking
- Budget tier considered: `low_cost`
- Policy: internal-first (`squads/etl-ops` + ETL infra before external tools)

## Phase 0 - Capability Gap Analysis

### Use Cases Analyzed
1. Quick channel/profile analysis
2. Deep competitive research
3. Framework benchmarking (AIOX vs competitors)
4. Trend monitoring

### Capability Coverage
- Fully covered (native/current): YouTube transcript/channel/metadata pipelines, web extraction, chunking/cleanup, report generation
- Partially covered: Instagram official enrichment, browser-grade capture evidence, benchmark timing standardization
- Gaps:
  - Instagram official API enrichment
  - dynamic browser capture for anti-bot pages
  - benchmark timing standard for comparisons

## Phase 1-5 - Discovered Tools

### Internal Stack Already Available (Primary)
1. `squads/etl-ops` task routing (`data/routing-profiles.yaml`)
2. `youtube-transcript.js` / `youtube-pipeline.js` / `youtube-metadata.js`
3. `fetch-page.js` for deterministic web extraction
4. ETL transformers/validators in squad contracts (`checkpoints.yaml`, `output-contract.yaml`)

### MCP Servers (Fallback/Enhancement)
1. `@modelcontextprotocol/server-playwright` - browser automation and dynamic extraction
2. `firecrawl-mcp` - robust crawling for difficult pages
3. `@apify/actors-mcp-server` - actor-based fallback for hard social targets

### APIs
1. YouTube Data API v3 - channel/video/search metadata
2. Apify API - social/web actor-based extraction
3. Meta Graph API (Instagram Platform) - profile/media insights (with app review constraints)

### CLI Tools
1. Internal ETL CLIs (`youtube-*`, `fetch-page`, `transcribe`, `ebook-to-markdown`) as default
2. `yt-dlp` - metadata fallback if needed by ETL profile
3. `hyperfine` - benchmark execution timing
4. `instaloader` - optional Instagram fallback

### Libraries
1. `youtube-transcript-api` (Python) - programmatic transcript fallback
2. `apify-client` (Python/JS) - controlled data extraction workflows
3. `playwright` (Node/Python) - scripted browser extraction and validation

### GitHub Projects
1. `modelcontextprotocol/servers`
2. `mendableai/firecrawl-mcp-server`
3. `jkawamoto/mcp-youtube-transcript`
4. `yt-dlp/yt-dlp`
5. `instaloader/instaloader`

## Phase 6 - Prioritization (Impact vs Effort)

### Quick Wins (implement now)
1. Wire `spy` tasks to `etl-ops` process profiles as first path
2. Standardize benchmark timing with `hyperfine`
3. Keep `yt-dlp` as explicit fallback only (already compatible with ETL)

### Strategic (plan next)
1. YouTube Data API v3 enrichment in `spy` outputs
2. Playwright MCP for dynamic pages and screenshot evidence
3. Apify API/MCP for difficult Instagram and anti-bot scenarios

### Fill-ins
1. `youtube-transcript-api` fallback path
2. `instaloader` local fallback when Graph API is not available

### Avoid for now
1. Full enterprise social suites with high recurring cost and overlap with existing scope

## Recommended Capability Mapping

| Capability | Primary | Fallback |
|---|---|---|
| youtube_transcripts | `etl-ops` + `youtube-transcript.js` | `yt-dlp`, `youtube-transcript-api` |
| youtube_metadata | `etl-ops` + `youtube-metadata.js` | YouTube Data API v3, `yt-dlp` |
| instagram_profile_capture | Meta Graph API | `instaloader`, Apify |
| dynamic_page_extraction | `etl-ops` + `fetch-page.js` | Playwright MCP, `firecrawl-mcp` |
| benchmark_timing | `hyperfine` | shell `time` |
| deep_web_research | `exa` + `etl-ops` `fetch-page.js` | `web_fetch`, `firecrawl-mcp` |

## Risks and Constraints
- Meta Graph API coverage depends on app permissions and review path.
- Instagram extraction without official API can break with platform changes.
- API costs/rate limits should be budget-guarded in automation loops.

# Tool Integration Plan - Research Squad

## Objective
Increase analysis depth, reduce manual research time, and improve benchmark reproducibility for `spy`.
Execution policy: internal-first (use `etl-ops`/ETL infra first, external tools only as fallback).

## Implementation Waves

### Wave 1 (Immediate: 1-2 days)
1. Route `quick-analysis` and `deep-research` through `squads/etl-ops` profiles (`youtube_video`, `youtube_channel`, `web_page`).
2. Use ETL CLIs as default source layer (`youtube-transcript.js`, `youtube-metadata.js`, `fetch-page.js`).
3. Keep `yt-dlp` only as fallback path in extraction profiles.
4. Add `hyperfine` to benchmark-related tasks (`bench-*`) for deterministic timing evidence.

### Wave 2 (Short-term: 3-7 days)
1. Integrate YouTube Data API v3 enrichment (channel, video, engagement metadata).
2. Add Playwright MCP path for dynamic pages/screenshots only when ETL page fetch is insufficient.
3. Add Apify fallback for difficult social extraction paths.

### Wave 3 (Optional: 1-2 weeks)
1. Integrate Meta Graph API flows where account/app permissions allow.
2. Add `youtube-transcript-api` and `instaloader` as explicit fallback adapters.

## Proposed Task Wiring
- `quick-analysis`: `etl-ops` (`youtube_video`/`youtube_metadata`) + optional YouTube Data API
- `deep-research`: `etl-ops` (`web_page`/`youtube_channel`) + optional Apify fallback
- `bench-framework`: `hyperfine` + ETL evidence capture (+ Playwright only when needed)
- `bench-quick-compare`: ETL metadata pulls + transcript summary

## Environment Variables
- `YOUTUBE_API_KEY`
- `META_ACCESS_TOKEN`
- `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY`
- `APIFY_TOKEN`

## Success Metrics
1. >=30% reduction in manual research steps for deep research.
2. >=25% faster benchmark execution setup.
3. >=90% of analyses include source-backed metadata or transcript evidence.

## Validation Checklist
- [ ] `etl-ops` routing profile selected for each spy use case
- [ ] Internal ETL path executed before any external fallback
- [ ] Fallback path defined for each external dependency
- [ ] Rate-limit and cost guardrails documented
- [ ] At least one benchmark run with timing artifacts
- [ ] Output templates updated to include tool provenance

## Referência: references/squad/examples/sample-executive-summary.md

# Deep Research: Video Background Loops com IA (Marco 2026)

## Executive Summary

Pesquisa tecnica profunda sobre o estado da arte em geracao de video loops seamless com IA para uso em websites. Cobre modelos, APIs, tecnicas de loop, custos e pipeline recomendado.

**Classificacao:** UC-001 (Technical Deep Dive) + UC-002 (Strategic Decision Support)

**Confianca geral:** ALTA (baseada em documentacao oficial de APIs, pricing publico, e testes documentados por terceiros)

---

## Findings Principais

1. **Luma Ray 2 e o unico modelo com parametro `loop: true` nativo na API.** Todos os outros requerem tecnicas auxiliares (first-last-frame ou ffmpeg post-processing).

2. **Veo 3.1 suporta first-frame + last-frame via Gemini API**, permitindo loops seamless ao passar a mesma imagem como primeiro e ultimo frame. Qualidade cinematografica superior, mas custo alto ($0.40/s).

3. **Kling O1 (fal.ai) e a melhor relacao custo-qualidade para loops.** Suporta dual-keyframe (mesma imagem = loop perfeito) a $0.112/s com qualidade cinematografica excelente.

4. **Wan 2.1 FLF2V (fal.ai) e a opcao open-source mais barata** para first-last-frame a $0.20-0.40/video, mas qualidade inferior aos modelos proprietarios.

5. **Pipeline recomendado:** Gemini (imagem) -> Kling O1 ou Veo 3.1 (video com first=last frame) -> ffmpeg crossfade polish -> ffmpeg web optimization (H.264/VP9, <2MB).

6. **Custo por loop de 5s:** Desde $0.20 (Wan) ate $2.00 (Veo 3.1 4K). Sweet spot: Kling O1 a ~$0.56 por 5s.

---

## Indice dos Relatorios

|---------|----------|
| `01-models-comparison.md` | Comparacao detalhada de todos os modelos de video |
| `02-loop-techniques.md` | Tecnicas de loop: first-last-frame, crossfade, nativo |

| `06-sources.md` | Todas as fontes consultadas |

---

**Modelo:** Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context)
**Pipeline:** DR Orchestrator > UC-001 + UC-002 > Synthesis

# 01 - Comparacao de Modelos de Video IA (Marco 2026)

## Panorama Geral

O mercado de geracao de video por IA em marco de 2026 oferece 10+ modelos viáveis para image-to-video via API. Para o caso de uso especifico de **video background loops para websites**, os criterios criticos sao:

1. Suporte a image-to-video (i2v)
2. Capacidade de loop seamless (nativo ou via first-last-frame)
3. Qualidade cinematografica do movimento
4. Custo por geracao
5. Resolucao e duracao

---

## Tier S: Melhor Qualidade Cinematografica

### Google Veo 3.1

- **Provedor:** Google (Gemini API / Vertex AI)
- **Modelo:** `veo-3.1-generate-preview`
- **I2V:** Sim (image como first frame)
- **First-Last-Frame:** Sim (parametro `lastFrame` no config)
- **Loop nativo:** Nao (mas first=last frame produz loop seamless)
- **Resolucao:** 720p, 1080p, 4K
- **Duracao:** 4s, 6s, 8s
- **Audio:** Gerado nativamente junto com video
- **Qualidade:** A mais alta do mercado para realismo, estabilidade de movimento, agua, fogo, particulas. "Closest thing to true AI cinematography."
- **Custo:** $0.40/segundo (standard), $0.15/segundo (Fast)
- **Latencia:** 11 segundos a 6 minutos
- **Watermark:** SynthID (invisivel)
- **Limitacao:** Videos expiram em 2 dias no servidor

### Google Veo 3

- **Modelo:** `veo-3-generate-preview`
- **I2V:** Sim
- **First-Last-Frame:** NAO (apenas Veo 3.1)
- **Resolucao:** 720p, 1080p
- **Custo:** $0.40/segundo
- **Nota:** Sem suporte a lastFrame. Para loops, usar Veo 3.1.

---

## Tier A: Excelente Custo-Qualidade

### Kling O1 (First-Last-Frame)

- **Provedor:** Kuaishou, via fal.ai
- **Endpoint fal.ai:** `fal-ai/kling-video/o1/image-to-video`
- **I2V:** Sim
- **First-Last-Frame:** Sim (dual-keyframe nativo)
- **Loop nativo:** Sim, ao usar mesma imagem como first e last frame
- **Resolucao:** 720p, 1080p
- **Duracao:** 5s, 10s
- **Qualidade:** Excelente. "Strongest balance of physical accuracy, visual quality, stability." Otimo para texturas, iluminacao, tecidos.
- **Custo:** $0.112/segundo
- **Vantagem para loops:** A mesma imagem como first e last frame gera "perfect seamless infinite loop" automaticamente.

### Kling 2.5 Turbo Pro / Kling 2.6 Pro

- **Endpoint fal.ai:** `fal-ai/kling-video/v2.5/turbo-pro/image-to-video`
- **I2V:** Sim
- **First-Last-Frame:** Nao (apenas Kling O1)
- **Custo:** $0.07/segundo (2.5 Turbo), $0.07-0.14/s (2.6 Pro)
- **Qualidade:** Muito alta. Motion fluidity excelente.
- **Nota:** Para loops, precisa de ffmpeg post-processing.

### Kling 3.0

- **Provedor:** Kuaishou, via fal.ai
- **Status:** Lancado em 2026, disponivel no fal.ai
- **Qualidade:** "State-of-the-art, built for structured storytelling"
- **Nota:** Verificar se herda suporte a dual-keyframe do O1.

---

## Tier A: Loop Nativo

### Luma Ray 2 (Dream Machine)

- **Provedor:** Luma Labs
- **API:** `POST /dream-machine/v1/generations`
- **I2V:** Sim (via keyframes: frame0, frame1)
- **Loop nativo:** SIM (`"loop": true` na API)
- **First-Last-Frame:** Sim (frame0 + frame1)
- **Resolucao:** 540p, 720p, 1080p, 4K
- **Duracao:** 5s
- **Modelos:** Ray 2 Flash (rapido, barato), Ray 2 (alta qualidade)
- **Camera control:** Linguagem natural no prompt ("camera orbit left")
- **Custo API:** $0.20/task (Ray 2 Flash), $0.50/task (Ray 2)
- **Custo subscription:** 11 credits/s (Flash), 32 credits/s (Standard)
- **Vantagem unica:** UNICO modelo com `loop: true` nativo na API. Zero post-processing necessario.
- **Limitacao:** Qualidade de movimento ligeiramente inferior a Veo/Kling para cenas complexas.

---

## Tier B: Opcoes Solidas

### Runway Gen-4 Turbo

- **Provedor:** Runway
- **API:** Publica, sem aprovacao necessaria (gerar API key no portal)
- **I2V:** Sim
- **First-Last-Frame:** Nao documentado
- **Loop nativo:** Nao
- **Resolucao:** 720p, 1080p
- **Duracao:** 5s, 10s
- **Custo:** 5 credits/segundo = $0.05/segundo (Gen-4 Turbo)
- **Nota:** Gen-4.5 = 12 credits/s ($0.12/s), Gen-4 Aleph = 15 credits/s ($0.15/s)
- **Vantagem:** Muito barato. Bom para prototipagem rapida.
- **Limitacao para loops:** Requer ffmpeg crossfade. Camera control menos preciso que Kling.
- **Curiosidade:** Runway tambem oferece Veo 3/3.1 via sua API (40 credits/s).

### Pika v2.2

- **Provedor:** Pika, via fal.ai
- **Endpoint:** `fal-ai/pika/v2.2/image-to-video`
- **I2V:** Sim
- **Loop nativo:** Nao
- **Resolucao:** 720p ($0.20), 1080p ($0.45)
- **Duracao:** 5s
- **Qualidade:** Boa para movimento suave, mas inferior a Kling/Veo em realismo.
- **Nota:** Ja configurado no setup existente.

### Wan 2.1 FLF2V (First-Last-Frame-to-Video)

- **Provedor:** Alibaba (open-source), via fal.ai
- **Endpoint:** `fal-ai/wan-flf2v`
- **I2V:** Sim
- **First-Last-Frame:** SIM (parametros start_image_url + end_image_url)
- **Resolucao:** 480p ($0.20), 720p ($0.40)
- **Frames:** 81-100 (default 81, ~5s a 16fps)
- **Inference steps:** 2-40 (default 30)
- **Qualidade:** Boa para o preco, mas visivelmente inferior a modelos proprietarios.
- **Vantagem:** Mais barato do mercado. Open-source (self-hostavel).
- **Limitacao:** 720p maximo. Pode ter artefatos em movimentos complexos.

### Wan 2.5 I2V

- **Provedor:** Alibaba, via fal.ai
- **Endpoint:** `fal-ai/wan-i2v`
- **Custo:** $0.05/segundo (480p)
- **First-Last-Frame:** Nao (apenas Wan 2.1 FLF2V)
- **Nota:** Versao mais nova, mas sem suporte a dual-keyframe.

---

## Tier C: Alternativas

### Hailuo 2.3 Pro
- $0.49/video (1080p) via fal.ai
- Qualidade boa, sem suporte a loop nativo

### Minimax Video-01
- $0.50/video via fal.ai
- Sem loop nativo

### Pixverse v3.5
- $0.30-0.80/video via fal.ai
- Sem loop nativo

### Stable Video Diffusion (Replicate)
- Open-source, muito barato (~$0.007/run)
- Qualidade baixa, max 4 segundos, sem loop
- Ultrapassado em 2026

---

## Matriz Resumo: Suporte a Loop

| Modelo | Loop Nativo | First-Last-Frame | Requer ffmpeg |
|--------|-------------|-------------------|---------------|
| Luma Ray 2 | SIM (`loop: true`) | SIM | NAO |
| Veo 3.1 | NAO | SIM (`lastFrame`) | Opcional |
| Kling O1 | NAO | SIM (dual-keyframe) | Opcional |
| Wan 2.1 FLF2V | NAO | SIM | Opcional |
| Runway Gen-4 | NAO | NAO | SIM |
| Pika v2.2 | NAO | NAO | SIM |
| Kling 2.5/2.6 | NAO | NAO | SIM |
| Wan 2.5 | NAO | NAO | SIM |

---

## Ranking para Background Loops de Website

1. **Kling O1 via fal.ai** - Melhor overall. Dual-keyframe com mesma imagem = loop perfeito. Custo razoavel. Qualidade excelente.
2. **Luma Ray 2** - Mais facil (loop nativo). Bom para automacao total. Qualidade levemente inferior.
3. **Veo 3.1 via Gemini API** - Melhor qualidade absoluta. Custo alto. Ideal para hero sections premium.
4. **Wan 2.1 FLF2V via fal.ai** - Mais barato. Qualidade aceitavel para backgrounds sutis.
5. **Runway Gen-4 Turbo** - Barato, mas requer ffmpeg para loop. Sem first-last-frame.
