```yaml
workflow:
  phases:
    2_generate_prompt:
      name: "Gerar Prompt de Deep Research"
      description: |
        Transforma query + context em prompt estruturado.
        Uses inferred_context from Phase 0 (auto-clarification) when available:
        - inferred_context.focus → determines research angle (technical, comparison, general)
        - inferred_context.temporal → adds year constraints to searches if "recent"
        - inferred_context.domain → scopes research to specific technologies
        If manual clarification was used (Phase 1), merge those answers with inferred_context.

        When decomposition_result is available (from Phase 1.5):
        - Use decomposition_result.sub_queries to generate more targeted research prompts
        - Each sub-query becomes a focused search vector instead of a single broad query
        - decomposition_result.main_topic provides the central theme for the research prompt
        - decomposition_result.search_strategy ("parallel"|"sequential") informs execution order
        When decomposition_result is NOT available (backward compatibility):
        - Use the original single query as before (no behavior change)
      template: "deep-research-prompt-template.md"
      output: "01-deep-research-prompt.md"
```


## Referência: references/squad/workflows/tech-research/phase-3-2-deep-read.yaml

````yaml
workflow:
  phases:
    3_2_deep_read:
      toc:
        - "1. Select sources for deep read"
        - "2. Route by URL/content type"
        - "3. Extract relevant content"
        - "4. Append progress checkpoint rows"
        - "5. Return enriched results"
      name: "Deep Page Reading (ETL + WebFetch)"
      # MODEL TIER: HAIKU (via Task tool or within subagent context)
      # In v3, deep reads are typically performed WITHIN each subagent
      # during Phase 3 dispatch. This phase is used as a SUPPLEMENTAL pass
      # for the orchestrator if additional deep reads are needed after
      # subagent results are aggregated, or as FALLBACK if subagent dispatch fails.
      description: |
        For top 3-5 most relevant search results, extract full content.
        Uses ETL service for YouTube and blogs (FREE, PRIMARY), WebFetch for others.
        This provides deeper information than search snippets alone.
        In v3.2, deep reads happen in the main runtime by default. Optional
        subagents may assist only when the runtime exposes them.
        This phase runs supplementally if the orchestrator needs more depth.

      execution: |
        1. IDENTIFY TOP RESULTS to read deeply:
           - Sort search_results by:
             a. Credibility level (HIGH > MEDIUM > LOW)
             b. Relevance to query (title/snippet match)
             c. Content promise (looks detailed, has code)
           - Select top 5 results (or fewer if <5 HIGH/MEDIUM available)

        2. CATEGORIZE URLS BY EXTRACTION METHOD:

           a. YOUTUBE URLS (use ETL - FREE):
              - Detect: youtube.com/watch, youtu.be/
              - Extract videoId from URL
              - Use CLI: node services/etl/bin/youtube-transcript.js {videoId} --format json
              - OR if Node available: ETL.extractYouTube(videoId)
              - Benefits: Free, 100% success, full transcript with timestamps

           b. PDF URLS (use ETL PDFCollector - FREE):
              - Detect: *.pdf, arxiv.org/pdf/, research papers
              - Download: curl -sL "{url}" -o /tmp/research_{slug}.pdf
              - Extract: node -e "
                const {PDFCollector} = require('./services/etl/collectors/pdf-collector');
                new PDFCollector().collect('/tmp/research_{slug}.pdf', '/tmp').then(r => console.log(JSON.stringify(r)));
                "
              - Benefits: FREE, pdftotext (poppler) primary, pdf-parse fallback
              - If scanned PDF (content < 50 chars): skip, note in gaps

           c. BLOG/ARTICLE URLS (use ETL CLI - FREE, PRIMARY):
              - Detect domains: dev.to, medium.com, marktechpost.com, hashnode.dev,
                hackernoon.com, freecodecamp.org/news, blog.*, *.blog.*, any article URL
              - PRIMARY: ETL fetch-page CLI:
                ```bash
                node services/etl/bin/fetch-page.js {url}
                ```
              - FALLBACK 1: mcp__exa__crawling(url) (if Exa available)
              - FALLBACK 2: WebFetch
              - Benefits: Platform detection (WordPress/Medium/generic), clean markdown,
                blocklist filtering (257 domains), no API costs
              - Exit code 1 = blocked domain → skip (do NOT retry with WebFetch)
              - Exit codes 2-4 → try fallbacks

           d. OTHER URLS (use ETL fetch-page PRIMARY):
              - All remaining URLs
              - PRIMARY: node services/etl/bin/fetch-page.js {url}
              - FALLBACK: WebFetch with prompts/page-extract.md
              - Timeout: 30s per page

        3. EXECUTE EXTRACTIONS:

           FOR YouTube URLs:
           ```bash
           # CLI method (always works)
           node services/etl/bin/youtube-transcript.js {videoId} --format json > /tmp/transcript_{videoId}.json
           ```

           FOR PDF URLs:
           ```bash
           curl -sL "{url}" -o /tmp/research_{slug}.pdf && node -e "
             const {PDFCollector} = require('./services/etl/collectors/pdf-collector');
             new PDFCollector().collect('/tmp/research_{slug}.pdf', '/tmp').then(r => console.log(JSON.stringify(r)));
           "
           ```

           FOR Blog/Article URLs (ETL CLI PRIMARY):
           ```bash
           # PRIMARY: fetch-page CLI (outputs markdown to stdout, status to stderr)
           node services/etl/bin/fetch-page.js {url} > /tmp/article_{slug}.md
           # JSON format with metadata:
           node services/etl/bin/fetch-page.js {url} --format json
           ```
           ```
           # Exit code 1 = blocked domain → skip entirely
           # Exit codes 2-4 → FALLBACK 1: mcp__exa__crawling(url) if Exa available
           #                → FALLBACK 2: WebFetch(url)
           ```

           FOR Other URLs:
           - PRIMARY: node services/etl/bin/fetch-page.js {url}
           - FALLBACK: Load prompts/page-extract.md + WebFetch

        3b. BLOG DISCOVERY (conditional, after initial reads):
           - IF a blog source is HIGH credibility AND covers research topic:
             → Use BlogDiscovery.discoverPosts(blogRootUrl) to find more posts
             → Filter by keyword relevance, take top 5
             → Only trigger if coverage < 70% and blog is authoritative
           - IF coverage already > 85%: skip discovery

        3c. LONG CONTENT CHUNKING (for content > 5000 chars):
           - Use SemanticChunker with strategy: paragraph (default)
           - Keep only chunks relevant to research query
           - Discard boilerplate, ads, unrelated sections

        4. EXTRACT STRUCTURED CONTENT:
           - Key findings with specific data
           - Code examples (preserved exactly, not paraphrased)
           - Expert quotes with attribution
           - For YouTube: speaker identification, timestamps for key points
           - Cross-reference notes (confirms/contradicts/adds vs other sources)

        5. HANDLE FAILURES:
           - YouTube: Should not fail (ETL has 100% success rate)
           - Blogs: Try ETL CLI (fetch-page.js) → WebFetch → skip
           - Exit code 1 = blocked domain (skip, don't retry with WebFetch)
           - Exit code 2-4 = try WebFetch fallback
           - Other: WebFetch → skip
           - Minimum 2 successful reads to proceed

        6. MERGE with search_results:
           - Enrich entries with extracted content
           - Tag extraction_method: "etl_youtube" | "etl_pdf" | "etl_blog_cli" | "webfetch"
           - Update credibility based on actual content quality

        7. Pass enriched_results to Phase 3.5 (evaluate coverage)

      tool_selection:
        youtube: "ETL.extractYouTube (FREE, 100% success)"
        blogs: "ETL fetch-page.js CLI (FREE, platform detection) → WebFetch fallback"
        docs: "WebFetch with page-extract.md prompt"
        other: "WebFetch"

      skip_when:
        - "Quick mode (*quick command)"
        - "All search results are LOW relevance"
        - "Coverage already at 80%+ from Context7/Exa alone"

      max_pages: 5
      timeout_per_page: 30000

      output: |
        {
          "enriched_results": [...],
          "extraction_stats": {
            "youtube_transcripts": N,
            "blog_etl": N,
            "webfetch": N,
            "failed": N
          }
        }
````


## Referência: references/squad/workflows/tech-research/phase-3-5-evaluate-coverage.yaml

````yaml
workflow:
  phases:
    3_5_evaluate_coverage:
      name: "Coverage Evaluation"
      # MODEL TIER: MAIN MODEL orchestration + deterministic worker scripts.
      description: |
        Avalia se a pesquisa está completa. Decide: continuar buscando ou parar.
        Loop: Phase 3 (search) → Phase 3.5 (evaluate) → CONTINUE/STOP
        Uses rigorous stopping criteria based on coverage score, source quality, and diminishing returns.

      execution: |
        1. Load prompts/evaluate.md for scoring framework

        2. Calculate metrics for this wave using Worker scripts:

           a. coverage_score — USE WORKER:
              ```bash
              echo '{"fundamentals":0.9,"implementation":0.7,"comparison":0.8,"best_practices":0.75,"real_world":0.6,"current_state":0.85}' | python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/coverage_calculator.py coverage
              ```
              Returns coverage_score + coverage_breakdown (6 dimensions, 0-100 each).
              IMPORTANT (Q1): Pass coverage_breakdown to Phase 5 for README metadata.

           b. source_quality — USE WORKER:
              ```bash
              echo '[{"url":"...","title":"...","pub_date":"..."}]' | python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/credibility_scorer.py --stdin
              ```
              Returns HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW counts + average_multiplier.
              Also count sources WITH pub_date vs WITHOUT (Q2 freshness).

           c. new_info_ratio — USE WORKER:
              ```bash
              python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/coverage_calculator.py newinfo --new {N} --total {M}
              ```
              - New facts = specific data points, techniques, perspectives NOT seen before
              - NOT new = same fact rephrased, same fact from different source

        3. Apply STOPPING RULES via Worker:
           ```bash
           echo '{"coverage":82,"newinfo":0.45,"wave":1,"high_sources":5}' | python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/coverage_calculator.py stop
           ```
           Returns {"decision":"CONTINUE|STOP","reason":"...","rule":"HARD_STOP|SOFT_STOP|CONTINUE"}
           Use the Worker's decision. Rules encoded in coverage_calculator.py:

           HARD STOPS (always stop):
           - wave >= 3 → "Max iterations reached"
           - coverage_score >= 85 AND high_credibility_sources >= 3 → "Sufficient quality coverage"
           - new_info_ratio < 0.10 for 2 consecutive waves → "Diminishing returns confirmed"

           SOFT STOPS (stop with caveat):
           - coverage_score >= 70 AND wave >= 2 → "Acceptable coverage achieved"
           - All high_priority gaps have failed searches → "Gaps not addressable via search"

           MUST CONTINUE:
           - coverage_score < 50 AND wave == 1 → "Insufficient first wave"
           - high_priority_gaps > 0 AND wave < 3 AND new_info_ratio > 0.15 → "Critical gaps remain addressable"

        4. IF CONTINUE:
           - Generate 2-4 targeted queries for specific gaps (not generic re-searches)
           - Use alternative phrasings if previous queries for same gap failed
           - Add specificity (versions, years, frameworks)

        5. IF STOP:
           - Document final coverage_score and any remaining gaps
           - Note if SOFT STOP (add caveat to final report)
           - Emit a concrete stop_reason using one of these categories:
             saturation, decision_sufficiency, max_waves, budget_limit,
             source_unavailable, authority_handoff, human_decision_required
           - Do not use vague stop reasons such as "complete" or "enough"

        6. UPDATE curiosity queue:
           - Add every high-impact unresolved gap to curiosity_queue.yaml
           - Mark questions resolved when this wave answered them
           - Mark questions discarded only with an explicit reason

        7. SCORE binary rubrics (minimum viable):
           - information_recall: facts/sources required by the scope
           - analysis: comparisons, trade-offs, counterevidence, implications
           - presentation: TL;DR, metadata, source traceability, next steps
           - Output passed/total counts for Phase 5 metadata

      output: |
        {
          "decision": "CONTINUE|STOP",
          "coverage_score": 0-100,
          "new_info_ratio": 0.0-1.0,
          "high_credibility_sources": N,
          "stop_reason": "reason if STOP",
          "stop_reason_category": "saturation|decision_sufficiency|max_waves|budget_limit|source_unavailable|authority_handoff|human_decision_required",
          "rubrics": {
            "information_recall": {"passed": N, "total": N},
            "analysis": {"passed": N, "total": N},
            "presentation": {"passed": N, "total": N}
          },
          "gaps": [...],
          "next_queries": [...] (if CONTINUE)
        }
````


## Referência: references/squad/workflows/tech-research/phase-3-6-compress-wave.yaml

````yaml
workflow:
  phases:
    3_6_compress_wave:
      name: "Wave Memory Compression"
      # MODEL TIER: MAIN MODEL structured summarization by default.
      description: |
        Compresses current wave results into a structured summary file.
        Runs AFTER Phase 3.5 evaluate, BEFORE next wave or synthesis.
        Solves context accumulation: waves 2+ read only summaries, not raw data.

        Pattern: Anthropic "structured note-taking" adapted for file-based persistence.
        - Wave results compressed into a concise structured summary
        - Saved to output dir as wave-{N}-summary.md
        - Next wave reads previous summaries instead of carrying raw results
        - Phase 4 (synthesis) reads ALL wave summaries for consolidated input

      execution: |
        TRIGGER: Runs after EVERY Phase 3.5 evaluation (both CONTINUE and STOP decisions).

        1. COLLECT current wave data:
           - search_results from this wave (URLs, titles, credibility tags)
           - key_findings extracted during deep reads
           - coverage_score and gaps from Phase 3.5
           - new_info_ratio for this wave
           - extraction_stats (tools used, success/fail counts)

        2. COMPRESS with this prompt:
           ```
           Compress these research results into a structured summary.
           Keep ONLY information needed for synthesis. Be ruthless about cutting redundancy.

           WAVE DATA:
           {wave_results_json}

           OUTPUT FORMAT (markdown, max 400 tokens):
           ## Wave {N} Summary
           **Coverage:** {score}/100 | **New Info:** {ratio} | **Sources:** {count} HIGH, {count} MEDIUM
           **Decision:** {CONTINUE|STOP} - {reason}

           ### Key Findings (max 7, one line each)
           1. {finding with specific data point} [source_url]
           2. ...

           ### Sources (URL + credibility only)
           - {url} (HIGH|MEDIUM) - {one-line what it contributed}

           ### Gaps Remaining
           - {gap description} (priority: HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW)

           RULES:
           - Each finding MUST have a specific fact (number, name, technique) - no vague summaries
           - Deduplicate: if 3 sources say the same thing, keep the best source only
           - Preserve exact numbers, tool names, version numbers
           - Do NOT include raw page content or full extractions
           ```

        3. SAVE to output directory:
           - File: {output_dir}/wave-{N}-summary.md
           - This file persists on disk even if session context is lost

        3b. UPDATE MARKOVIAN OPERATIONAL STATE:
           - File: {output_dir}/evolving_report.md
           - Rewrite it after every wave as the current bounded synthesis.
           - It must supersede the previous operational state rather than append raw history.
           - Keep wave-{N}-summary.md files as audit trail, not as the primary runtime state.
           - Include:
             - Current synthesis
             - Open questions pulled from curiosity_queue.yaml
             - Claims that changed confidence this wave
             - Stop readiness with explicit stop_reason if available

        4. CONTEXT MANAGEMENT (the key optimization):
           - After saving, the orchestrator can DISCARD raw wave results from working memory
           - For next wave: read evolving_report.md plus the latest summary instead of carrying raw data
           - For synthesis: read evolving_report.md first, then wave-*-summary.md files for audit trail

        BACKWARD COMPATIBILITY:
        - If file write fails: keep compressed text in context variable instead
        - Phase 4 MUST work with either compressed summaries OR raw results

      output: |
        wave-{N}-summary.md saved to output directory
        evolving_report.md updated as bounded operational state
        ~400 tokens per wave (vs ~5000 tokens raw data per wave)
        3 waves max = ~1200 tokens total vs ~15000 tokens raw
````


## Referência: references/squad/workflows/tech-research/phase-3-7-playwright-deep-research.yaml

```yaml
workflow:
  phases:
    3_7_playwright_deep_research:
      toc:
        - "1. Manual/deep trigger validation"
        - "2. Browser target availability"
        - "3. Query external LLMs"
        - "4. Aggregate responses"
        - "5. Write supplemental artifact"
      name: "Playwright Deep Research (Multi-LLM)"
      # MODEL TIER: MAIN MODEL - requires browser automation orchestration
      # MCP DEPENDENCY: playwright (mcp__playwright__*)
      description: |
        Browser automation phase that queries multiple LLMs (Grok, Claude.ai, Gemini)
        for deep research when traditional search doesn't achieve sufficient coverage.
        Uses Playwright MCP for browser control.

        TRIGGER CONDITIONS:
        - coverage_score < 70% after wave 2 (auto-trigger)
        - User passes --deep flag (manual trigger)
        - Query contains "multiple perspectives", "compare LLMs" (pattern match)

        GRACEFUL DEGRADATION:
        - If one LLM fails, continue with others
        - Partial output is better than no output
        - Minimum 1 successful LLM for valid output

      execution: |
        1. PRE-FLIGHT CHECK:
           - Test Playwright MCP availability:
             mcp__playwright__browser_navigate(url="https://example.com")
           - If fails: log "[PLAYWRIGHT] MCP unavailable", skip this phase

        2. DETERMINE TRIGGER:
           - Check coverage_score from Phase 3.5
           - Check for --deep flag in original query
           - Check for trigger keywords in query

           IF NOT TRIGGERED: skip to Phase 4

        3. FOR EACH LLM (Grok, Claude.ai, Gemini):
           See prompts/playwright-deep-research.md for detailed workflow.

           a. NAVIGATE to LLM URL
              Tool: mcp__playwright__browser_navigate
              Args: { url: "{llm_url}" }

           b. CHECK LOGIN STATE
              Tool: mcp__playwright__browser_snapshot
              Parse: Look for login indicators (user menu, avatar)

              IF NOT LOGGED IN:
                - Screenshot for evidence
                - Record error: "Not logged in to {llm}"
                - Continue to next LLM

           c. LOCATE AND FILL CHAT INPUT
              Try selectors in order (primary, fallback_1, fallback_2)
              Tool: mcp__playwright__browser_type
              Log which selector worked

           d. SUBMIT QUERY
              Tool: mcp__playwright__browser_click
              Wait for response (poll every 2s, max 60s)

           e. EXTRACT RESPONSE
              Tool: mcp__playwright__browser_snapshot
              Parse response container text

           f. CAPTURE SCREENSHOT
              Tool: mcp__playwright__browser_take_screenshot
              Save to: {output_dir}/screenshot-{llm}.png

           g. RECORD RESULT
              {
                llm: "{llm_name}",
                success: true/false,
                response: "{text}",
                error: "{error_if_any}",
                timestamp: "{ISO_timestamp}",
                screenshot: "screenshot-{llm}.png",
                selectors_used: { input: "...", submit: "...", response: "..." }
              }

        4. AGGREGATE RESULTS:
           - Collect all LLM responses
           - Count successful vs failed
           - IF all failed: log warning, skip aggregation

        5. SYNTHESIZE COMPARISON:
           - Identify consensus points (mentioned by 2+ LLMs)
           - Identify divergent views (conflicting recommendations)
           - Generate reliability assessment

        6. GENERATE OUTPUT FILE:
           - File: {output_dir}/XX-llm-deep-research.md
           - Format: See prompts/playwright-deep-research.md for template
           - Include all screenshots as evidence

        7. UPDATE README:
           - Add new file to research folder README.md index

      config_reference: "config.yaml -> playwright_deep_research"
      prompt_reference: "prompts/playwright-deep-research.md"

      trigger_conditions:
        auto:
          - coverage_score < 0.70 after wave 2
          - confidence_score < 0.60 on key topics
        manual:
          - --deep flag in query
          - "*deep command"
        keywords:
          - "multiple perspectives"
          - "compare LLM views"
          - "cross-reference with LLMs"

      llm_targets:
        - name: grok
          url: https://grok.x.ai
          requires: X/Twitter login
        - name: claude
          url: https://claude.ai
          requires: Anthropic account
        - name: gemini
          url: https://gemini.google.com
          requires: Google account

      error_handling:
        not_logged_in: "Skip LLM, record error, continue with others"
        selector_not_found: "Try fallback selectors, log which worked"
        timeout: "Retry once with extended timeout, then skip"
        all_failed: "Log warning, skip phase, continue to synthesis"

      output: |
        {
          "llm_results": {
            "grok": { success: bool, response: str, ... },
            "claude": { success: bool, response: str, ... },
            "gemini": { success: bool, response: str, ... }
          },
          "consensus_points": [...],
          "divergent_points": [...],
          "screenshots": ["screenshot-grok.png", ...],
          "output_file": "XX-llm-deep-research.md"
        }
```


## Referência: references/squad/workflows/tech-research/phase-3-execute-research.yaml

````yaml
workflow:
  phases:
    3_execute_research:
      toc:
        - "1. Pre-check MCP availability"
        - "2. Determine search mode"
        - "3. Detect special content types"
        - "4. Load previous wave context"
        - "5. Execute sub-queries"
        - "6. Aggregate results"
        - "7. Handle failures"
        - "8. Emit wave checkpoint artifacts"
      name: "Executar Pesquisa com Tool Strategy (v3.2 - runtime-honest Agent default)"
      # MODEL TIER: MAIN MODEL by default; optional deep-researcher only when available.
      description: |
        Executa pesquisa com estratégia de ferramentas e checkpoints incrementais.
        O modelo principal executa as sub-queries por padrão. Se o runtime expõe
        `deep-researcher`, o agente pode usá-lo como otimização opcional; se não,
        não promete dispatch. Cada sub-query concluída escreve uma linha em
        wave-{N}-progress.jsonl para recuperação determinística após timeout.
        Ver prompts/tool-strategy.md para hierarquia de ferramentas.
        Ver prompts/executor-matrix.md para classificação de operações por modelo.
      sources:
        - Exa MCP (neural search, papers, GitHub - HIGH credibility)
        - Context7 MCP (official library docs - HIGH credibility)
        - ETL Service (YouTube transcripts, blog extraction - FREE)
        - WebSearch native (fallback - always available)
      execution: |
        ## ORCHESTRATOR STEPS (MAIN MODEL - Opus/Sonnet)

        1. PRE-CHECK MCP AVAILABILITY:
           - Test Context7: mcp__context7__resolve-library-id("react", "test")
             → If fails, set context7_available = false
           - Test Exa: mcp__exa__web_search_exa("test query", 1)
             → If 401/429/503, set exa_available = false
           - Log availability for debugging

        2. DETERMINE SEARCH MODE:
           - IF decomposition_result is available AND decomposition_result.sub_queries exists:
             → queries_to_search = decomposition_result.sub_queries
           - IF decomposition_result is NOT available (backward compatibility):
             → queries_to_search = [original_user_query]

        3. DETECT SPECIAL CONTENT TYPES (per sub-query, before dispatch):

           PRE-STEP: Use url_detector Worker for any URLs found in sub-queries:
           ```bash
           echo '["url1","url2"]' | python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/url_detector.py --stdin
           ```
           This classifies URLs as youtube/github/arxiv/blog/generic BEFORE LLM dispatch.
           Use the classification to route each URL to the correct extraction method below.

           a. YOUTUBE DETECTION (type == "youtube"):
              - VideoId already extracted by url_detector (ids.id_0)
              → Use: ETL extractYouTube (FREE, 100% success)
              → CLI: node services/etl/bin/youtube-transcript.js {videoId}
              → Tag as: source: youtube_transcript, credibility: HIGH (1.2x)

           b. LIBRARY DETECTION (from inferred_context.domain):
              - IF context7_available AND library detected:
                → Use: mcp__context7__resolve-library-id + mcp__context7__query-docs
                → Tag as: source: official_docs, credibility: HIGH (1.3x)
              - FALLBACK: WebSearch with "site:{library}.dev docs"

           c. ACADEMIC/PDF DETECTION (SCHOLARLY-FIRST routing — STORY-154.2):
              - IF inferred_context.focus == "academic" OR
                query matches regex: arxiv|pubmed|paper|study|trial|cohort|systematic review|meta-analysis|peer-reviewed:

                PRIMARY — Scholarly adapter routing (PREFERRED over WebSearch for academic queries):
                → Call: python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/scholarly_search.py --query "{query}" --adapters arxiv,pubmed,semantic-scholar --max-results 5
                → Tag as: source: scholarly_adapter, credibility: HIGH (1.4x)
                → If scholarly_search.py exits 0 and returns results: USE as primary source set
                → If scholarly_search.py exits non-zero or returns empty: fall through to Exa

                SECONDARY — Exa research paper fallback:
              - IF exa_available AND (scholarly adapter returned < 3 results OR unavailable):
                → Use: mcp__exa__research_paper_search(query, numResults=5)
                → Tag as: source: academic_exa, credibility: HIGH (1.3x)
              - FALLBACK: WebSearch with "site:arxiv.org OR site:scholar.google.com"

              - FOR PDF URLs in results (*.pdf, arxiv.org/pdf/):
                → Download: curl -sL "{url}" -o /tmp/research_{slug}.pdf
                → Extract: PDFCollector.collect() (pdftotext primary, pdf-parse fallback)
                → If scanned PDF (content < 50 chars): skip, note in gaps
                → Tag as: source: pdf_extraction, credibility: HIGH (1.3x)

           d. GITHUB DETECTION:
              - IF query contains: github, repo, repository, code example
              - IF exa_available:
                → Use: mcp__exa__github_search(query, numResults=5)
                → Tag as: source: github, credibility: HIGH (1.2x)
              - FALLBACK: WebSearch with "site:github.com"

           e. GENERAL TECHNICAL QUERIES:
              - IF exa_available:
                → Use: mcp__exa__web_search_exa(query, numResults=10)
                → Tag as: source: exa_search, credibility: HIGH (1.2x)
              - FALLBACK: WebSearch(query)
                → Tag as: source: web_search, credibility: MEDIUM (1.0x)

        4. LOAD PREVIOUS WAVE CONTEXT (wave 2+ only):
           - IF this is wave 2 or later:
             → Read wave-*-summary.md files from output directory
             → These contain compressed findings from previous waves
             → Use gaps_remaining from last wave summary to focus new queries
             → DO NOT reload raw results from previous waves (they were compressed)
           - IF this is wave 1: skip this step

        5. EXECUTE SUB-QUERIES:
           - Default execution is main-context Agent search. Do not promise Haiku
             dispatch unless the `deep-researcher` subagent is actually available
             in the current runtime.
           - If the runtime exposes `deep-researcher`, dispatch sub-queries in
             parallel and aggregate JSON responses.
           - If it does not, execute sequentially in main context and record
             `subagent_stats.fallback_sequential`.
           - After EACH sub-query result set, append a JSONL checkpoint row to:
             `wave-{N}-progress.jsonl`
             Required row fields:
             `{timestamp, wave, sub_query, tool_used, sources_count, status}`.
           - On stream timeout or user `continue`, read the latest
             `wave-{N}-progress.jsonl`, skip completed sub-queries, and resume
             from the first missing sub-query.

           WORKER PROMPT TEMPLATE:
           ```
           WORKER_MODE: true

           Search for this specific sub-query and return structured findings.
           Use your MEMORY.md knowledge to optimize search and skip bad sources.

           QUERY: {sub_query}
           CONTEXT: {inferred_context_json}
           MCP AVAILABILITY: {exa_available: bool, context7_available: bool}

           INSTRUCTIONS:
           1. Consult your Source Quality Cache to know which domains are reliable
           2. Search using the best available tool:
              - If exa_available: use mcp__exa__web_search_exa(query, numResults=5)
              - Else: use WebSearch(query)
           3. From results, select top 2-3 most relevant URLs (skip LOW quality domains from memory)
           4. Deep-read the top 1-2 results using ETL-first approach:
              - YouTube URLs: Bash: node services/etl/bin/youtube-transcript.js {videoId} --format json
              - PDF URLs (arxiv.org/pdf/, *.pdf): download with curl, extract with PDFCollector
              - Blog/Article URLs: Bash: node services/etl/bin/fetch-page.js {url}
                (exit code 1 = blocked domain, skip; exit 2-4 = fallback)
              - Other URLs: Bash: node services/etl/bin/fetch-page.js {url}
                (fallback: WebFetch only if fetch-page fails)
           5. For long content (>5000 chars): use SemanticChunker to extract only relevant sections
           6. Extract key findings from each read page
           7. Score credibility using your cached source quality knowledge

           RETURN FORMAT (JSON only, no other text):
           {
             "sub_query": "the original sub-query",
             "sources": [
               {"url": "...", "title": "...", "snippet": "...",
                "credibility": "HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW", "tool_used": "..."}
             ],
             "key_findings": ["finding1", "finding2", "..."],
             "extraction_stats": {
               "youtube": 0, "blog_etl": 0, "pdf_etl": 0, "webfetch": 0, "exa": 0, "chunked": 0, "failed": 0
             }
           }

           IMPORTANT: Do NOT update your MEMORY.md in worker mode.
           Do NOT run full pipeline (decompose/synthesize/document). Just search and return.
           ```

           BACKWARD COMPATIBILITY:
           If Task(subagent_type: "deep-researcher") fails, fall back to
           sequential execution in main context and keep the progress JSONL
           checkpoint current.

        6. AGGREGATE RESULTS (MAIN MODEL):
           - Collect all subagent responses
           - Parse JSON output from each Task result
           - Deduplicate by URL (keep highest credibility version)
           - SCORE CREDIBILITY via Worker (instead of LLM scoring):
             ```bash
             echo '[{"url":"...","title":"...","pub_date":"..."}]' | python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/credibility_scorer.py --stdin
             ```
             Use the Worker's HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW + multiplier output for source quality.
             This replaces LLM-based credibility assessment with deterministic regex patterns.
           - Build unified search_results with tool attribution
           - Combine extraction_stats across all subagents

        7. HANDLE FAILURES:
           - For each failed subagent (no response or invalid JSON):
             → Log warning: "Subagent for sub-query '{query}' failed"
             → Execute that sub-query sequentially in main context as fallback
           - For each failed MCP call within subagents:
             → Subagent should have already applied fallback chain
           - RULE: At least 1 successful result (from any subagent) to proceed

        8. Pass enriched_results to Phase 3.2 (if deep reads needed) or 3.5 (evaluate)
        9. Ensure `wave-{N}-progress.jsonl` exists before Phase 3.5. Missing progress
           checkpoint is a recoverability failure.
      output: |
        {
          "search_results": [...],
          "tools_used": {"exa": N, "context7": N, "etl": N, "websearch": N},
          "mcp_availability": {"exa": bool, "context7": bool},
          "credibility_breakdown": {"high": N, "medium": N, "low": N},
          "subagent_stats": {"dispatched": N, "succeeded": N, "failed": N, "fallback_sequential": N}
        }
````


## Referência: references/squad/workflows/tech-research/phase-4-5-verify-citations.yaml

````yaml
workflow:
  phases:
    4_5_verify_citations:
      # MODEL TIER: MAIN MODEL (Opus/Sonnet) - requires semantic verification
      name: "Citation Verification"
      description: |
        Verify all claims in the synthesized report have traceable sources.
        Based on Anthropic's multi-agent research pattern where a dedicated
        agent processes documents to attribute all claims to sources.

      execution: |
        1. Load prompts/verify-citations.md

        2. Extract factual claims using Worker (deterministic regex extraction):
           ```bash
           python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/claim_extractor.py extract < {output_dir}/02-research-report.md
           ```
           Returns claims with type (statistic, numeric, comparison, benchmark, ranking, market, count).
           The Worker handles regex extraction. The LLM handles semantic verification below.

        3. Match claims to sources using Worker (string matching):
           ```bash
           echo '{"claims":[...],"sources":[...]}' | python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/claim_extractor.py match
           ```
           Returns MATCHED/UNSOURCED per claim + match_score.

        4. Cross-reference each claim against search_results (LLM semantic verification):
           - For MATCHED claims: verify source actually says what we claim
           - For UNSOURCED claims: add caveat or remove
           - Check for paraphrasing that changes meaning

        4. Classify each claim:
           - VERIFIED: Source found, claim accurate
           - PARAPHRASED: Meaning slightly altered
           - MISATTRIBUTED: Source says something different
           - UNSOURCED: No source in collection
           - OUTDATED: Source older than 2 years on changing topic

        5. Calculate integrity_score:
           integrity_score = (verified + paraphrased) / total_claims * 100

        6. TAG CLAIMS WITH CONFIDENCE (Q3):
           For each factual claim in the report that includes numbers, comparisons,
           or definitive statements, add an inline confidence tag:
           - [HIGH — N sources]: Claim supported by 2+ HIGH credibility sources
           - [MEDIA — N sources]: Claim supported by 1 HIGH or 2+ MEDIUM sources
           - [LOW — N sources]: Claim supported by 1 MEDIUM or only LOW sources
           - [UNSOURCED]: No supporting source found (add caveat or remove)
           Example: "Custo estimado de $0.06-$0.12 [MEDIA — baseado em token budgets, não medição real]"
           Example: "Playwright é o padrão dominante [HIGH — 3 projetos + npm 3.1M/week]"

        7. Generate fixes:
           - IF integrity_score < 70%: Flag report as "LOW INTEGRITY - Review Required"
           - FOR each MISATTRIBUTED/UNSOURCED: Add caveat or remove
           - FOR each PARAPHRASED: Suggest rewrite

        8. Pass verified_report + integrity_score + claim counts to Phase 5 (Document)

      output: |
        {
          "integrity_score": 0-100,
          "total_claims": N,
          "verified": N,
          "issues": [...],
          "verified_report": "report with fixes applied"
        }

      skip_when:
        - "Quick mode (*quick command)"
        - "Report has fewer than 5 factual claims"
````


## Referência: references/squad/workflows/tech-research/phase-4-synthesize.yaml

````yaml
workflow:
  phases:
    4_synthesize:
      # MODEL TIER: MAIN MODEL (Opus/Sonnet) - requires deep reasoning for synthesis
      name: "Sintetizar"
      description: |
        Consolidar todos os findings em recomendações práticas.
        CRITICAL: Produz DOCUMENTAÇÃO ONLY, nunca código de produção.

        In v3.1+: Reads wave summary files (from Phase 3.6) instead of raw results.
        This keeps synthesis context clean and focused on key findings only.

      execution: |
        1. READ Markovian state and wave summaries:
           - Read evolving_report.md first as the current operational state
           - Read ALL wave-*-summary.md files from output directory
           - If no summary files exist (backward compat): use raw results from context
           - Merge findings across waves, noting which wave provided each finding

        2. DEEP DIVE on top players/frameworks (Q8 — Depth):
           When research covers a MARKET or COMPETITIVE LANDSCAPE:
           - Identify the top 3-5 most relevant players, frameworks, or papers
           - For each, provide a dedicated subsection with:
             a. What it does (features, architecture, capabilities)
             b. What it does NOT do (limitations, gaps)
             c. Insight for the user's context (how it relates to their project/squad)
           - This prevents "mention without depth" — every key player gets proper analysis
           - If total players > 10, tier them: Tier 1 (deep analysis) vs Tier 2 (brief mention)

        3. DOMAIN-AWARE synthesis (Q9 — Context Mapping):
           When the user's query references a SPECIFIC PROJECT, SQUAD, or SYSTEM:
           - Identify the user's domain entities (e.g., agents, components, modules)
           - Map findings to those entities explicitly
           - Example: if user has agents RADAR/GATE/THESIS/SCORER/CRITIC,
             map each finding to the agent it informs
           - This bridges "what exists in the market" → "what it means for YOUR system"
           - If no domain context provided, skip this step

        4. SCOPE DECLARATION (mandatory for category/comparison queries):
           When the query implies a set of entities (alternatives, tools, builders,
           frameworks, libraries, platforms, vendors, approaches), include a
           `scope_declaration` block in `02-research-report.md`:
           ```yaml
           scope_declaration:
             requested_category: "<category named or implied by user>"
             inclusion_criteria: ["criterion 1", "criterion 2"]
             included_in_report: ["entity 1", "entity 2"]
             excluded_with_reason:
               - entity: "<entity>"
                 reason: "out_of_scope | low_corpus_coverage | different_subcategory | not_yet_evaluated"
           ```
           If the report narrows the universe without this block, Phase 5 validator
           must fail the run.

        5. Sintetizar em relatório completo

        5.5 EXTRACT QUICK WINS (mandatory):
           Pós-síntese, varrer todos os findings consolidados e selecionar
           o subconjunto que satisfaça simultaneamente:
             - value = high (com benefício observável: métrica, redução de custo,
               eliminação de bug, ganho de coverage, etc.)
             - effort ∈ {XS (~1h), S (~4-8h)} — NUNCA M, L, XL
             - time_to_value ≤ 1 semana

           Para cada Quick Win, registrar:
             - target_type: squad | app | skill | agent | runner | rule | workflow | adr | doc
             - target_path: caminho exato no hub (ex: `squads/sinkra-squad/`,
               `.claude/skills/tech-research/`, `apps/squad-engine/`, etc.)
             - evidence: § ou subseção de 02-research-report.md que ancora o QW
             - definition_of_done: critério verificável binário
             - action_owner: @pm | @dev | @architect | @qa | @devops

           REGRAS DE INTEGRIDADE:
             - Mínimo de 3 QW. Se < 3 candidatos legítimos, NÃO inventar —
               documentar `## Quick Wins Não Encontrados` em quick-wins.md
               com candidates_evaluated, candidates_qualified, reasoning.
             - QW que não cabem no critério vão para 03-recommendations.md
               §Implementation Roadmap (effort > S) ou §Ranking (value não-high).
             - NÃO duplicar QW dentro de 03-recommendations.md — quick-wins.md
               é o lar canônico do subconjunto ROI-first.

        6. STOP REASON + OPEN QUESTIONS:
           - Include `## Stop Reason` in 02-research-report.md
           - State why research stopped using the Phase 3.5 stop_reason
           - Include unresolved high-impact questions or explicitly state none remain
           - If unresolved high-impact questions remain, status must be PASS_WITH_OPEN_ITEMS

        7. SEMPRE terminar com "Próximos Passos" recomendando @pm, @architect, @dev, @qa ou @devops conforme autoridade

      deliverables:
        - Lista de técnicas rankeadas
        - Deep dives nos top 3-5 players/frameworks (com limitações e insights)
        - Código de REFERÊNCIA (apenas para documentação)
        - Domain mapping (quando contexto de projeto/squad fornecido)
        - Stop reason and unresolved open questions
        - Próximos passos práticos
        - Quick Wins set (≥3 OR documented gap) — feeds Phase 5 quick-wins.md

      output: "draft_report + quick_wins_set (internal, passed to verification)"
````


## Referência: references/squad/workflows/tech-research/phase-5-document.yaml

````yaml
workflow:
  phases:
    5_document:
      toc:
        - "1. Scaffold output directory"
        - "2. Write README metadata"
        - "3. Write report and recommendations"
        - "4. Save mandatory metrics/state"
        - "5. Run blocking output validator"
      # MODEL TIER: MAIN MODEL (Opus/Sonnet) - requires structured writing
      name: "Documentar"
      description: "Salvar estrutura completa com research metadata e quality indicators"
      structure:
        folder: "docs/research/{YYYY-MM-DD}-{slug}/"
        files:
          - "README.md (índice + research_metadata)"
          - "00-query-original.md"
          - "01-deep-research-prompt.md"
          - "02-research-report.md"
          - "03-recommendations.md"
          - "quick-wins.md"
      execution: |
        ## PRE-STEP: Scaffold output directory (Worker — deterministic)

        BEFORE writing any content, run the scaffold Worker to create the folder
        and stub files with correct template structure:
        ```bash
        python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/scaffold.py --slug "{slug}" --title "{title}" --query "{query}" --date {YYYY-MM-DD}
        ```
        This guarantees identical structure every time, regardless of model or session.
        The Worker is idempotent — safe to re-run (never overwrites existing files).
        After scaffolding, OVERWRITE the stub files with actual content using Write/Edit tools.

        ## QUALITY REQUIREMENTS (v4 improvements Q1-Q7)

        ### README.md — MUST include Research Metadata block (Q1+Q7)
        After the TL;DR section, include a ```yaml block with:
        - workflow_version (must match SKILL.md workflow_version)
        - runtime_contract with workflow_version, schema_version, skill_version, tool_contract_version
        - coverage_score (total 0-100)
        - coverage_breakdown with 6 dimensions from evaluate.md:
          fundamentals, implementation, comparison, best_practices, real_world, current_state
          Each scored 0-100 (convert from dimension_scores in Phase 3.5)
        - integrity_score (from Phase 4.5 citation verification, or "N/A" if skipped)
        - sources.total, sources.high_credibility, sources.medium_credibility
        - sources.with_dates (count of sources where publication date was identified)
        - sources.freshness_ratio (with_dates / total, as percentage)
        - waves (number of search waves executed)
        - citation_verified (true OR skipped_with_reason: "...")
        - stop_reason (explicit reason from Phase 3.5)
        - rubrics with information_recall, analysis, presentation passed/total counts
        See templates/output-structure.md for exact format.

        ### 02-research-report.md — Claims with confidence tags + source dates (Q2+Q3)
        Factual claims that include numbers, comparisons, or definitive statements
        MUST include inline confidence tags: [HIGH — N sources], [MEDIA — N sources], [LOW — N sources]
        Example: "Framework X is used by 3 of 4 audited projects [HIGH — 3 sources]"
        Example: "Custo estimado de $0.06-$0.12 por pesquisa [MEDIA — baseado em token budgets, não medição real]"

        SOURCE DATES IN REFERENCES (Q2 enforcement):
        In the References section at the end of the report, EVERY source MUST include
        its publication date (year minimum, month if available) inline next to the URL.
        Format: `[Title](url) — YYYY` or `[Title](url) — YYYY-MM` or `[Title](url) — date_unknown`
        Example: `[Granted AI: 7 Tools Tested](https://grantedai.com/...) — 2026`
        Example: `[DINGO Ontology](https://dcodings.github.io/DINGO/) — 2020`
        Sources older than 24 months on fast-moving topics get an OUTDATED note.

        DEEP DIVES ON TOP PLAYERS (Q8 enforcement):
        When the research covers a MARKET, COMPETITIVE LANDSCAPE, or MULTIPLE FRAMEWORKS:
        The report MUST include dedicated subsections for the top 3-5 most relevant players.
        Each subsection follows this structure:
        ```
        ### N.N {Player/Framework Name}
        **Tier:** {1|2|3} — 1 = build/use now; 2 = reference/pattern; 3 = monitor/defer
        **Category:** {short-kebab-case category, e.g. native-runtime, reference-runtime, runner-foundation}
        **Role:** {what role this player has in the decision, e.g. delegation-runtime, prior-art, supervisor-template}
        **Fit:** {high|medium|low}
        **Action:** {concrete action this player implies for the user's project}
        **What it does:** {features, architecture, capabilities — 2-3 sentences}
        **What it does NOT:** {limitations, gaps — 2-3 sentences}
        **Insight for this context:** {how it relates to the user's question — 1-2 sentences}
        **Source:** {URL} — {YYYY}
        ```
        If >10 players: Tier 1 (top 5, deep dive) vs Tier 2 (remaining, brief table).
        Do NOT just list players in a comparison table without individual analysis.
        Do NOT rely on the section number as the tier. `### 2.1 Foo` inside
        `## 2. Players` is not automatically Tier 2; the explicit `**Tier:**`
        field is the authority.

        ### 03-recommendations.md — No overlap + effort estimates + domain mapping (Q5+Q6+Q9)
        - DO NOT repeat findings already in 02-research-report.md (max 20% overlap)
        - Sections: Decisão Recomendada, Ranking, Implementation Roadmap, Anti-Patterns, Próximos Passos
        - Every actionable recommendation MUST include effort estimate: S (~2h), M (~4-8h), L (~2-3d), XL (~1w+)
        - Implementation Roadmap table MUST include: Fase, Ação, Effort, Owner (@pm/@dev), Timeline
        - DOMAIN MAPPING (Q9): When the user's query references a specific project/squad/system,
          add a section "Mapping para o Projeto" with this EXACT table format:

          | Componente do Projeto | Finding Relevante | Ação Recomendada | Effort |
          |----------------------|-------------------|------------------|--------|
          | {agent/component 1}  | {specific finding} | {concrete action} | S/M/L/XL |

          Example rows:
          | GATE agent | FRAPO has 16 eligibility properties | Incorporate hasHeadcount, hasCountryCode in gate checks | M (~4h) |
          | CRITIC agent | D3 SAMRE uses iterative 4-round debate | Adapt SAMRE protocol for 4-mode specialized debate | L (~2d) |

          This section bridges "what the market/research says" → "what YOUR system should do".
          If no domain context in the query, skip this section entirely.
        See templates/output-structure.md for exact format.

        ### quick-wins.md — ROI-first subset (mandatory)
        Standalone document with the Quick Wins set produced in Phase 4 step 5.5.
        REQUIREMENTS:
        - File MUST exist as `quick-wins.md` in the output directory.
        - MUST contain `## Quick Wins Selecionados` with a markdown table; minimum 3 rows
          (rows starting with `| QW-1 |`, `| QW-2 |`, `| QW-3 |` or `| 1 |`, `| 2 |`, `| 3 |`).
        - Each QW row MUST list: name, target, type, value=high, effort=XS|S, time-to-value, evidence (§ of report), owner.
        - MUST include `## Detalhamento por Quick Win` with one block per selected QW
          (O quê, Onde, Por que alto valor, Por que baixo esforço, Evidência, Definition of Done, Riscos, Owner).
        - If less than 3 qualifying candidates exist, MUST include `## Quick Wins Não Encontrados`
          with the YAML diagnostics block (`quick_wins_minimum_met: false`, `candidates_evaluated`,
          `candidates_qualified`, `reasoning`, `remediation`). NEVER pad the table with low-quality items.
        - README.md Índice MUST list `quick-wins.md` (the scaffolder handles this; verify after writing).
        - TL;DR in README.md SHOULD reference the count of Quick Wins identified
          (e.g. "3 Quick Wins selecionados" or "0 Quick Wins — gap documentado").
        See templates/output-structure.md for exact format.

        ### POST-WRITE: Save metrics/state, then validate output (Workers)

        Before metrics/state, ensure these mandatory state artifacts exist:
        - curiosity_queue.yaml
        - evolving_report.md
        - execution-log.jsonl
        If this is a follow-up, resolve the next number with:
        ```bash
        python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/next_followup_number.py {output_dir}
        ```

        After writing all files, run these Workers in this exact order:

        1. SAVE METRICS + STATE (MANDATORY):
           ```bash
           echo '{"pipeline_id":"...","workflow_version":"1.1.0","runtime_contract":{"workflow_version":"1.1.0","schema_version":"research-output.v2","skill_version":"1.0.0","tool_contract_version":"manual"},"coverage_score":85,"coverage_breakdown":{...},"integrity_score":90,"citation_verified":true,"stop_reason":"decision_sufficiency: coverage threshold met and no high-impact open questions remain","rubrics":{"information_recall":{"passed":8,"total":10},"analysis":{"passed":5,"total":7},"presentation":{"passed":6,"total":6}},"sources":[...],"waves":1,"validator_result":"pending"}' | python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/metrics_collector.py save --dir {output_dir}
           ```
           Creates metrics.yaml and pipeline-state.yaml in the output directory.
           These files are mandatory. If either file is missing, the run is incomplete.

        2. VALIDATE OUTPUT (QG-PROD-6 — BLOCKING):
           ```bash
           python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/output_validator.py {output_dir}
           ```
           Checks: required files exist, confidence tags present, source dates in refs,
           workflow_version present, citation_verified present, metrics.yaml present,
           and pipeline-state.yaml present.
           If valid=false, fix missing files before completing. Do not present a
           completion message until the validator passes.

        3. EXTRACT SOURCES MANIFEST (deterministic, advisory) — QF-4:
           ```bash
           python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/sources_extractor.py {output_dir}
           ```
           Emits {output_dir}/sources.yaml: artifact-first source manifest with
           id, url, title, date, credibility (via credibility_scorer.py),
           first_seen_in (file), first_seen_section (markdown heading), and totals
           (by_credibility + with_date + date_coverage_ratio).
           Adopted from §5 padrão #5 of 02-research-report.md ("Source evidence
           drawer"). Allows downstream consumers (verify-citations, audit UI, the
           Observatory's source drawer) to operate on structured data instead of
           re-parsing markdown. Failure here is logged but does NOT block phase
           completion (the report is still valid without the manifest).

        4. EMIT UNIVERSAL RESEARCH PROFILE (deterministic, advisory) — EPIC-150:
           ```bash
           python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/research_profile.py {output_dir}
           ```
           Emits {output_dir}/research-profile.yaml with profile.type
           (tech|bench|market|product|mapping), dashboard labels, artifact policy,
           decision mode and Rubrica dimension pack. Must run before decision_rubric.py.
           Advisory; failure logged but does not block.

        5. EXTRACT PLAYERS MANIFEST (deterministic, advisory) — QF-D1:
           ```bash
           python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/players_extractor.py {output_dir}
           ```
           Emits {output_dir}/players.yaml: parses `### N.N Name` deep-dive blocks
           from 02-research-report.md (matching the phase-5 "DEEP DIVES ON TOP
           PLAYERS" template) into structured entries with what_it_does,
           what_it_does_not, insight, source (title+url+date), explicit tier,
           category, role, fit, action, and excluded flag. If explicit fields are
           absent, the extractor uses conservative heuristics.
           Allows the Observatory to render a filterable players grid instead of
           re-parsing markdown headings. Advisory; failure is logged but does not
           block phase completion.

        6. EXTRACT COMPARISON MATRICES (deterministic, advisory) — QF-D2:
           ```bash
           python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/comparison_matrix_extractor.py {output_dir}
           ```
           Emits {output_dir}/matrices.yaml: every markdown table directly under a
           `## N. ...` section becomes a structured matrix with `columns: [...]`
           and `cells: [{col: value, ...}]`. Inline tables inside `### N.N`
           player blocks are intentionally ignored. Unlocks heatmap / sortable
           comparison UI in the Observatory without re-parsing tables at view
           time. Advisory; failure logged but does not block.

        7. EXTRACT UX PATTERNS CATALOG (deterministic, advisory) — QF-D3:
           ```bash
           python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/ux_patterns_extractor.py {output_dir}
           ```
           Emits {output_dir}/ux-patterns.yaml: scans `## ...` sections whose
           title matches /padr(?:ões|ão|ao)|pattern/i and parses numbered bold
           items (`N. **Name:** Description`) into id+number+name+description+
           reference+section. Builds the per-research catalog. (Cross-research
           aggregate as `docs/research/_ux-patterns.json` is a separate skill —
           not yet wired here; tracked in curiosity_queue.) Advisory; failure
           logged but does not block.

        8. EXTRACT ACTION ASSETS (deterministic, advisory) — QF-D4:
           ```bash
           python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/action_assets_extractor.py {output_dir}
           ```
           Emits action-plan.yaml, claims.yaml, risk-register.yaml, decision-ledger.yaml.
           MUST run before research_graph.py — the graph reads claims and decisions from
           these artifacts to build richer edges. Advisory; failure logged but does not block.

        9. EMIT DECISION RUBRIC (deterministic, advisory) — EPIC-150:
           ```bash
           python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/decision_rubric.py {output_dir}
           ```
           Emits {output_dir}/decision-rubric.yaml with domain-specific dimensions,
           presets and rankings when at least two players exist. If fewer than two
           players are detected, it still writes `status: not_applicable` rather
           than inventing alternatives. Advisory; failure logged but does not block.

        10. BUILD MACHINE-READABLE RESEARCH GRAPH (deterministic, advisory) — DEPENDS ON steps 3-9:
           ```bash
           python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/research_graph.py {output_dir}
           ```
           Emits {output_dir}/research-graph.json with nodes (root/query/prompt/report/
           recommendations/followup/wave/quick_wins/evolving/curiosity/log/metrics/
           pipeline_state/source/player/claim/decision/action/risk/question) and edges
           (contains/produces/spawns_followup/checkpoint/derives/describes/indexes/
           supports/cited_in/analyzed_in/documents/informs/drives/recommends/constrains/
           open_item/raises/declares). Adopted from btahir/open-deep-research "Flow" pattern.
           Filesystem-first, zero LLM, zero network. Run AFTER sources, players, matrices,
           action_assets — graph quality improves with more artifacts present. Failure here
           is logged but does NOT block phase completion.

        11. EMIT LOCAL RESEARCH INTELLIGENCE CONTRACT (deterministic, advisory) — EPIC-150:
           ```bash
           python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/research_contract.py {output_dir}
           ```
           Emits {output_dir}/research-contract.json with research kind, decision
           context, taxonomy, unit of analysis, rubric method, evidence model and
           stop rules for this specific request. Must run after profile, rubric and
           graph. Advisory; failure logged but does not block.

        12. EMIT DASHBOARD MANIFEST + VALIDATION REPORT (deterministic, advisory) — EPIC-150:
           ```bash
           python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/dashboard_manifest.py {output_dir}
           ```
           Emits dashboard-manifest.yaml and validation-report.yaml. Must run after
           research_contract.py so validation can report the local contract status.
           Advisory; failure logged but does not block.

        13. REFRESH CROSS-RESEARCH KNOWLEDGE-BASE INDEX (deterministic, advisory):
           ```bash
           python3 squads/research/scripts/tech-research/research_kb_index.py --root docs/research
           ```
           Regenerates docs/research/_index.json by scanning all sibling research
           folders (slug, topic, date, coverage_score, sources, decision, status, tags).
           Adopted from btahir/open-deep-research Knowledge Base sidebar pattern.
           Idempotent (atomic write); failure here is logged but does NOT block phase
           completion. Useful for any downstream UI (Observatory, dashboards) and for
           detecting prior research before launching a new pipeline.
````


## Referência: references/squad/workflows/tech-research/tech-research-pipeline.yaml

```yaml
# Tech Research — Aggregate Pipeline Manifest (SINKRA-native v2.0.0)
# Source of truth: phase → operator-mode → outputs → checkpoint mapping.
# Pattern: aligned with squads/sinkra-squad/workflows/sinkra-pipeline.yaml
# Consumed by: .claude/skills/tech-research/SKILL.md (process_mapping pointer)

pipeline:
  id: SP-TECH-RESEARCH
  organism: ORG-TRR-001
  mode: EXPLORAR
  version: "2.0.0"
  sinkra_version: "1.2"
  description: |
    Deep technical research pipeline with multi-wave search, coverage scoring,
    multi-LLM cross-reference, and citation verification. 7 molecules, 11 atoms.

execution_model:
  pattern: inline_persona_fidelity
  rationale: |
    Persona-fidelity inline (not spawned subagents). The skill itself plays
    each persona in main context, loading the phase workflow YAML + prompt
    before executing. TeamCreate is used for visual task tracking only —
    no Agent() subagent_type spawn is required.
  visual_tracking:
    team_name_pattern: "trr-{slug}"
    task_create: true
    task_update_per_phase: true

learning_log:
  rule: incremental-learning-log
  path_pattern: ".aiox/learning/logs/tech-research/{slug}-{timestamp}.yaml"
  initialize_at: P00c
  update_at: per_phase
  finalize_at: P5b
  schema_version: "1.0"

phases:

  # ============ INITIALIZATION (team-lead, inline) ============
  - id: P00
    name: Parse Args + Initialize
    persona: team-lead
    execution: inline
    inputs: [user_query, flags]
    outputs:
      - original_query
      - inferred_flags
      - output_dir
      - start_epoch
    next: P00b

  - id: P00b
    name: Create Team + Tasks
    persona: team-lead
    execution: inline
    tools: [TeamCreate, TaskCreate]
    outputs: [team_name, task_ids]
    next: P00c

  - id: P00c
    name: Initialize Incremental Learning Log
    persona: team-lead
    execution: inline
    rule_applied: incremental-learning-log
    outputs:
      - learning_log_yaml   # pre-populated with all phases as status:pending
    next: P0

  # ============ M1: AUTO-CLARIFY ============
  - id: P0
    name: Auto-Clarify
    persona: research-decomposer (inline)
    molecule: M1
    workflow_ref: squads/research/workflows/tech-research/phase-0-auto-clarify.yaml
    data_refs:
      - squads/research/data/tech-research/auto-clarification.yaml
    outputs:
      - inferred_context     # SEED for P1: focus, technology, temporal_intent
    next: P1

  - id: P1
    name: Strategic Brief Builder
    persona: research-decomposer (inline)
    execution: always        # no skip path — always builds the strategic brief
    workflow_ref: squads/research/workflows/tech-research/phase-1-clarify.yaml
    data_refs:
      - squads/research/data/tech-research/auto-clarification.yaml
    outputs:
      - strategic_brief       # structured Deep Research brief (code block)
      - clarifying_questions  # 2-3 questions, outside the code block
    next: P1.5

  # ============ M2: DECOMPOSE ============
  - id: P1.5
    name: Decompose Brief (2-3 sub-queries per SCOPE angle)
    persona: research-decomposer (inline)
    molecule: M2
    workflow_ref: squads/research/workflows/tech-research/phase-1-5-decompose.yaml
    prompt_ref: squads/research/prompts/tech-research/decompose.md
    inputs:
      - strategic_brief        # from P1; SCOPE angles → sub-queries
    outputs:
      - decomposition_result   # N sub-queries (2-3 per SCOPE angle, 5-18; PD mode 5-7)
    next: P2

  # ============ M3: GENERATE PROMPT ============
  - id: P2
    name: Generate Deep Research Prompt
    persona: research-prompter (inline)
    molecule: M3
    workflow_ref: squads/research/workflows/tech-research/phase-2-generate-prompt.yaml
    template_ref: squads/research/templates/tech-research/deep-research-prompt-template.md
    outputs:
      - research-prompt        # docs/research/{date}-{slug}/01-deep-research-prompt.md
    next: P3

  # ============ M4: EXECUTE RESEARCH (waves loop) ============
  - id: P3
    name: Execute Research Wave
    persona: research-executor (inline)
    molecule: M4
    workflow_ref: squads/research/workflows/tech-research/phase-3-execute-research.yaml
    data_refs:
      - squads/research/data/tech-research/dependencies.yaml
    prompt_refs:
      - squads/research/prompts/tech-research/tool-strategy.md
      - squads/research/prompts/tech-research/executor-matrix.md
    outputs:
      - search_results
      - wave-{N}-progress.jsonl
    loop: per_wave           # up to 3 waves
    next: P3.2

  - id: P3.2
    name: Deep Read Top Sources (supplemental)
    persona: research-executor (inline)
    molecule: M4
    execution: conditional   # only when snippets insufficient
    workflow_ref: squads/research/workflows/tech-research/phase-3-2-deep-read.yaml
    prompt_ref: squads/research/prompts/tech-research/page-extract.md
    outputs:
      - enriched_results
    next: P3.5

  - id: P3.5
    name: Evaluate Coverage [COVERAGE_GATE]
    persona: coverage-evaluator (inline)
    molecule: M4
    workflow_ref: squads/research/workflows/tech-research/phase-3-5-evaluate-coverage.yaml
    prompt_ref: squads/research/prompts/tech-research/evaluate.md
    checkpoint: COVERAGE_GATE
    outputs:
      - coverage_score
      - coverage_breakdown
      - source_quality
      - remaining_gaps
      - decision   # stop | continue | escalate-multi-llm
    verdict_routing:
      stop_continue: P3.6
      stop_done: P4
      continue: P3   # next wave (max 3 total)
      veto: HALT     # COVERAGE_GATE VETO — escalate to user
    next: P3.6

  - id: P3.6
    name: Compress Wave Summary
    persona: coverage-evaluator (inline)
    molecule: M4
    workflow_ref: squads/research/workflows/tech-research/phase-3-6-compress-wave.yaml
    outputs:
      - wave-{N}-summary.md
      - evolving_report.md       # updated cumulative state
    next_when_continue: P3
    next_when_stop: P3.7_or_P4

  - id: P3.7
    name: Playwright Multi-LLM Deep Research (escape valve)
    persona: research-executor (inline)
    molecule: M4
    execution: conditional   # --deep flag OR coverage<70 after wave 2 OR manual trigger
    workflow_ref: squads/research/workflows/tech-research/phase-3-7-playwright-deep-research.yaml
    prompt_ref: squads/research/prompts/tech-research/playwright-deep-research.md
    config_ref: .claude/skills/tech-research/config.yaml#playwright_deep_research
    mcp_required:
      - playwright (graceful degradation if absent)
    outputs:
      - llm-deep-research   # XX-llm-deep-research.md
    next: P4

  # ============ M5: SYNTHESIZE ============
  - id: P4
    name: Synthesize Findings + Extract Quick Wins
    persona: research-synthesizer (inline)
    molecule: M5
    workflow_ref: squads/research/workflows/tech-research/phase-4-synthesize.yaml
    inputs:
      - wave_summaries
      - llm_deep_research (if present)
      - enriched_results
    outputs:
      - synthesis_draft
      - quick-wins         # docs/research/{date}-{slug}/quick-wins.md (≥3 items OR gap block)
    rules:
      - quick_wins: "value=high ∧ effort ∈ {XS, S} ∧ time_to_value ≤ 1 week"
      - preserve_disagreement: true   # never flatten contradictions
    next: P4.5

  # ============ M6: VERIFY CITATIONS [CITATION_GATE] ============
  - id: P4.5
    name: Verify Citation Integrity [CITATION_GATE]
    persona: citation-verifier (inline)
    molecule: M6
    workflow_ref: squads/research/workflows/tech-research/phase-4-5-verify-citations.yaml
    prompt_ref: squads/research/prompts/tech-research/verify-citations.md
    checkpoint: CITATION_GATE
    outputs:
      - citation_integrity_report
      - fixes_applied
    verdict_routing:
      approve: P5
      review: P5_with_caveats   # document unsupported claims with explicit caveat
      veto: P4_redo             # back to synthesis with fix queue (max 2 attempts)
    next: P5

  # ============ M7: DOCUMENT (split into 5.0 narrative + 5.1 extractors) ============
  - id: P5.0
    name: Write Narrative Atoms (hand-authored Markdown + YAML)
    persona: research-documenter (inline)
    molecule: M7
    workflow_ref: squads/research/workflows/tech-research/phase-5-document.yaml
    template_refs:
      - squads/research/templates/tech-research/output-structure.md
      - squads/research/templates/tech-research/output-structure.yaml
    outputs:
      - research-readme       # README.md
      - original-query        # 00-query-original.md
      - research-report       # 02-research-report.md
      - recommendations       # 03-recommendations.md
      - curiosity-queue       # curiosity_queue.yaml (schema: items: [{question,status,owner?}])
      - metrics.yaml
      - pipeline-state.yaml
    next: P5.1

  - id: P5.1
    name: Run Extractor Atoms (apps/research rich render tier)
    persona: research-documenter (inline)
    molecule: M7
    execution: deterministic_scripts
    extractors:
      - script: squads/research/scripts/tech-research/sources_extractor.py
        emits: sources           # sources.yaml
        consumed_by: [Evidências, Fontes]
      - script: squads/research/scripts/tech-research/players_extractor.py
        emits: players           # players.yaml
        consumed_by: [Players]
      - script: squads/research/scripts/tech-research/ux_patterns_extractor.py
        emits: ux-patterns       # ux-patterns.yaml (empty_allowed)
        consumed_by: [Map]
      - script: squads/research/scripts/tech-research/comparison_matrix_extractor.py
        emits: matrices          # matrices.yaml (empty_allowed)
        consumed_by: [Map]
      - script: squads/research/scripts/tech-research/logger.py
        action: consolidate
        emits: execution-log     # execution-log.jsonl (consolidates wave-*-progress.jsonl)
        consumed_by: [Waves]
      - script: squads/research/scripts/tech-research/research_graph.py
        emits: research-graph    # research-graph.json
        depends_on: [sources]    # must run AFTER sources_extractor
        consumed_by: [Evidências, Map]
    failure_mode: warn_and_continue   # extractor failure does NOT halt pipeline; downgrades render tier to `partial`
    next: P5_validate

  - id: P5_validate
    name: Validate Output
    persona: research-documenter (inline)
    validator: squads/research/scripts/tech-research/output_validator.py
    halt_on_invalid: true
    next: P5b

  - id: P5b
    name: Finalize Learning Log + Suggest Next Command
    persona: team-lead
    execution: inline
    rule_applied:
      - incremental-learning-log   # mark outcome:completed, set timestamp_completed
      - cli-next-command-flow      # suggest next logical command (skip if --yolo)
    outputs:
      - learning_log.outcome = completed
      - next_command_suggestion
    next: DONE

  - id: HALT
    name: Halt with Reason
    persona: team-lead
    execution: inline
    triggers: [veto, user_abort, missing_required_file, no_results_after_fallback]
    actions:
      - learning_log.outcome = halted|failed|escalated
      - learning_log.timestamp_completed = now
      - emit halt_report to user with reason + remediation hint

# ============ ARTIFACT INDEX ============
# Mirrors config.yaml artifact_contracts[] for fast lookup.
artifacts:
  required_narrative:            # P5.0 — hand-authored
    - research-readme            # P5.0
    - original-query             # P5.0
    - research-prompt            # P2
    - research-report            # P5.0
    - recommendations            # P5.0
    - quick-wins                 # P4 (≥3 items OR documented gap block)
    - curiosity-queue            # P5.0
    - evolving-report            # P3 (updated each wave)
    - wave-summary               # P3 (cardinality: many, 1 per wave)
    - metrics                    # P5.0 — metrics.yaml
    - pipeline-state             # P5.0 — pipeline-state.yaml
    - learning-log               # P00c→P5b (incremental, OUT of output_dir → .aiox/learning/logs/)
  required_extractors:           # P5.1 — apps/research rich render tier
    - sources                    # sources.yaml
    - players                    # players.yaml
    - ux-patterns                # ux-patterns.yaml (empty_allowed)
    - matrices                   # matrices.yaml (empty_allowed)
    - execution-log              # execution-log.jsonl (consolidated)
    - research-graph             # research-graph.json (depends on sources)
  conditional:
    - llm-deep-research          # P3.7 (only when triggered)

# ============ CHECKPOINTS ============
checkpoints:
  - id: COVERAGE_GATE
    phase: P3.5
    veto_when: "coverage_score < 50 after max_waves=3"
    review_when: "50 ≤ coverage_score < 70"
    approve_when: "coverage_score ≥ 70"
    escape_valve: P3.7
  - id: CITATION_GATE
    phase: P4.5
    veto_when: "verified_citation_ratio < 0.85 after 2 fix attempts"
    review_when: "verified_citation_ratio ≥ 0.85 AND unsupported_claim_count > 0"
    approve_when: "verified_citation_ratio ≥ 0.85 AND unsupported_claim_count == 0"

# ============ INVOKES ============
invokes_downstream:
  - skill: /research-chief
    condition: "--product-discovery flag OR auto-clarify detects product_validation pattern"
    purpose: "feeds atoms 3 (Villain OSINT) + 4 (WTP signals) of spy validate-product-idea molecule"

invoked_by_upstream:
  - skill: /research-chief
    relationship: research helper for product-discovery Wave 0
  - skill: /skill-creator
    relationship: optional prior-art evidence
  - skill: /aiox-architect
    relationship: optional research-before-decision

# ============ DOWNSTREAM RENDERERS ============
# apps/research Research Observatory consumes the artifacts written under
# docs/research/{date}-{slug}/ for visual exploration.
downstream_renderers:
  - target: apps/research/observatory/research
    contract: apps/research/HANDOFF-research-compatibility.md
    render_tiers:
      rich:
        when: "all required_narrative + all required_extractors present"
        unlocked_tabs: [Doc, Map, Evidências, Waves, Fontes, Players, Ações, Perguntas]
      partial:
        when: "narrative present + some extractors missing (typically research-graph or sources)"
        unlocked_tabs: [Doc, Map (partial), Waves, Ações, Perguntas]
      legacy:
        when: "only Markdown narrative — no extractor atoms"
        unlocked_tabs: [Doc, Ações]
    atom_to_tab:
      Doc:        [research-readme, research-report, recommendations]
      Map:        [metrics, pipeline-state, matrices, ux-patterns, curiosity-queue, research-graph]
      Evidências: [sources, research-graph, metrics]
      Waves:      [execution-log, wave-summary]
      Fontes:     [sources]
      Players:    [players]
      Ações:      [recommendations, quick-wins, curiosity-queue]
      Perguntas:  [curiosity-queue]
```
